1.title: My pet peeves
1.brief: Write a paragraph about the habits that get on your nerves. Use it-clauses with “when” to react to them and relative clauses to describe the people involved.
1.briefEs: Escribe un párrafo sobre los hábitos que te molestan usando cláusulas con “it… when” y cláusulas relativas.
criteria: Three it-clauses with when (It bothers me when…, I can’t stand it when…).
Two relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted (the people I live with).
Use “pet peeve” and “to get on someone’s nerves”.
1.model: Everybody has pet peeves, and I have quite a few. It really bothers me when people talk on the phone in the cinema. I also can't stand it when someone eats my food from the fridge without asking. The person I share a flat with does this all the time, and it gets on my nerves. Another thing is unpunctuality. It drives me crazy when friends who promise to arrive at eight turn up at nine without a message. On the other hand, I love it when people are considerate. A colleague who brings coffee for everyone on Monday morning is my hero! I think small details like these show who you can really trust.

1.title: A reference for a friend
1.brief: A friend is applying to share a flat. Write a short reference describing his or her personality and why he or she would be a good flatmate.
1.briefEs: Escribe una carta de referencia describiendo la personalidad de un amigo como buen compañero de vivienda.
criteria: Four personality adjectives from the unit (reliable, considerate, trustworthy…).
Three relative clauses with who, that or which.
Formal opening and closing (To whom it may concern / Yours faithfully).
1.model:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to recommend Felipe Rodríguez, who has been my friend and flatmate for three years. Felipe is one of the most reliable people that I know. He always pays the bills on time and he never forgets the cleaning rota. He is also very considerate: he keeps the music low when people are studying and he always asks before inviting guests. It is something I really appreciate when people respect shared spaces. He is trustworthy, too. When I travelled for two months, he looked after my plants and my cat, which was not easy! I am sure he would be an excellent flatmate.

Yours faithfully,
Laura Medina

1.title: The person I look up to
1.brief: Write a blog post about someone you look up to. Explain who the person is and describe a moment when you understood why you admire them.
1.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre alguien a quien admiras y un momento en que entendiste por qué.
criteria: Use “to look up to” and one more phrase from the unit.
Two relative clauses, one used as an object with the pronoun omitted.
One it-clause with when (It amazed me when…).
1.model: The person I look up to most is my older sister, Camila. She is a nurse who works night shifts at a public hospital in Bogotá. For years I didn't understand why she chose such a difficult job. Then, last year, my grandfather became very ill. Camila was the one who explained everything to the family calmly. It amazed me when she stayed awake for two days to help him. The patience she showed was incredible. She never complains about the people she works with, even when they drive her crazy. She is the kind of person everybody wants as a friend. Today I'm studying medicine, and that is because of her.

1.title: Flatmate wanted
1.brief: Write a forum post looking for a flatmate. Describe the kind of person you want with relative clauses and say what bothers you with it-clauses.
1.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro buscando compañero de piso: describe a la persona ideal con cláusulas relativas y lo que te molesta con “it… when”.
criteria: At least two defining relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted (The person I lived with…).
At least two it-clauses with when (It drives me crazy when…).
Use one adjective from the unit (reliable, considerate or trustworthy).
1.model:
Hi everyone,

I'm a second-year student at the University of Seville and I'm looking for a flatmate. I want someone who is reliable and who pays the bills on time. The person I lived with last year left dirty plates in the sink for days, and it drives me crazy when I come home to that. It also bothers me when people play loud music after midnight, because I get up at six for my part-time job. On the other hand, I love it when someone cooks for the group once a week! The flat that we're renting has three bedrooms and a small balcony, which is perfect for plants. If you think you're the right person, send me a message.

Thanks,
Irene

1.title: The Corner Café
1.brief: Write a review of a café, restaurant or shop you know. Use relative clauses to describe the people and things, and it-clauses to react to what you like and dislike.
1.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un café o una tienda que conozcas usando cláusulas relativas y “it… when” para tus reacciones.
criteria: At least three defining relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted.
At least two it-clauses with when (It gets on my nerves when…).
Use “to get on someone’s nerves” or “to drive someone crazy”.
1.model:
The Corner Café, Manchester

The Corner Café is a small place near the university that I visit every Friday. The staff are friendly, and the waiter who serves me always remembers my order. It's a relief when a café has fast wifi, and this one does! The coffee they use comes from a family farm in Colombia, and it tastes wonderful. The only problem is the noise. It gets on my nerves when the music is too loud, because I can't study. Another thing I can't stand is the queue at lunchtime, which sometimes reaches the door. Still, the cakes are the best I've ever tried. If you're looking for a place where you can relax with friends, I recommend it.

1.title: My summer workmates
1.brief: Write an email to a friend about the people at your summer job. Identify them with relative clauses and say what bothers you with it-clauses.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre las personas de tu trabajo de verano, con cláusulas relativas y “it… when”.
criteria: At least three relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted.
At least two it-clauses with when.
Use “reliable” and “to drive someone crazy”.
1.model:
Hi Tom,

How's the summer going? My job at the beach café is great, mainly because of the people. The manager is someone who really cares about the team. There's also a girl called Nina who is very reliable. She's the one I trust with the till. The only person I can't get along with is Marco, who arrives late every day. It drives me crazy when he leaves me to close the café alone. I wanted to tell him, but it's hard when you're the youngest one there. Anyway, the tips are good, and I've already saved 300 euros for our trip. Are you still planning to come in August? Let me know!

Best,
Carla

1.title: Phones at the dinner table
1.brief: Should phones be banned at the dinner table? Give your opinion, mention one opposing view and describe how you feel in different situations.
1.briefEs: ¿Deberían prohibirse los móviles en la mesa? Da tu opinión, menciona una postura contraria y describe tus reacciones con “it… when”.
criteria: At least three it-clauses with when (It annoys me when…, It’s rude when…).
At least two defining relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted.
One opposing view introduced with “Some people say that…”.
1.model:
Should phones be banned at the dinner table?

In my opinion, they should. Families who eat together have a chance to talk, and phones destroy that chance. It annoys me when my brother checks his messages in the middle of a conversation, because I feel ignored. It's also rude when someone answers a call while the food is getting cold. Some people say that a phone is useful for showing photos or looking up information. That is true, but it's something that can wait until after the meal. The rule we have at home is simple: everybody leaves their phone in a basket by the door. At first, my parents thought it was a strange idea, but now they love it. It's a pleasure when we all laugh at the same joke. I believe dinner is the one time of day that deserves our full attention.

1.title: Problems at FitZone Gym
1.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint to a gym or sports centre. Describe the problems with relative clauses and react to them with it-clauses.
1.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja a un gimnasio describiendo los problemas con cláusulas relativas y “it… when”.
criteria: At least two defining relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted.
At least two it-clauses with when.
Formal register: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam and Yours faithfully.
1.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the service at FitZone Gym in Leeds, where I have been a member since January. The machines I use most often are frequently out of order. It is frustrating when I arrive after a long day at work and find a sign on the treadmill. The instructor who runs the evening class is often late, and it annoys me when the session starts twenty minutes behind schedule. I also cannot accept the changing rooms, which are dirty and cold. The monthly fee is £35, and I believe this price should include a reliable service. I would be grateful if you could repair the equipment and reply within a week.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Hughes

1.title: A buddy scheme for new students
1.brief: Write a short proposal for a buddy scheme at your school or college. Explain the problem and the solution, identifying the people involved with relative clauses.
1.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta breve de un programa de “compañeros guía” para estudiantes nuevos, identificando a las personas con cláusulas relativas.
criteria: At least three defining relative clauses, one with the pronoun omitted.
At least one it-clause with when.
Clear headings: Introduction, The problem, The solution.
1.model:
Proposal: a buddy scheme for new students

Introduction
This proposal suggests a buddy scheme for students who join our college in September.

The problem
It is stressful when you arrive at a new college and you know nobody. Last year, several first-year students told me that they felt lost during the first month. The ones who had a friend in the building adapted much faster.

The solution
Each new student would be paired with a second-year student who is considerate and reliable. The buddy is the person newcomers can ask about timetables, rooms and clubs. Buddies would meet them on the first day and have lunch with them once a week for a month. It would also be a great experience for the older students, who could add it to their CV.

If the idea is approved, I can prepare the application form this week.

2.title: Learning online or in a classroom?
2.brief: Compare learning a language online and in a classroom. Give your opinion and support it with comparisons.
2.briefEs: Compara aprender un idioma en línea y en un salón de clase, y da tu opinión.
criteria: Start one sentence with a gerund phrase as subject (Studying online is…).
Five comparisons with adjectives, nouns and verbs (more flexible, fewer, as much as).
Use “advantage / drawback” and “by far” or “nowhere near”.
2.model: Learning a language is time-consuming, so choosing the right method is important. Studying online is far more flexible than going to a classroom: you can study at midnight if you want. It is also cheaper, and you waste less time travelling. However, the biggest drawback is motivation. Students who study alone usually practise less than students in a group, and they speak nowhere near as much. In a classroom, you get more feedback and you make friends. Talking to real people is by far the best way to lose your fear. In my opinion, the ideal option is a mix: online lessons for grammar and vocabulary, and face-to-face classes for speaking. That way you get the advantages of both.

2.title: Why I gave up social media
2.brief: Write a short article about a habit you gave up or took up. Explain why and compare your life before and after.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo corto sobre un hábito que dejaste o empezaste, comparando tu vida antes y después.
criteria: Two gerund phrases as subject and two as object.
Three comparisons (less stressed than, as … as, more time).
Use “to give up” or “to take up” and “worthwhile”.
2.model: Last year I decided to give up social media for six months. Scrolling through Instagram was taking up two hours of my day, and comparing my life with other people's made me feel worse. At first, not checking my phone was harder than I expected. But after a month, I felt much less stressed than before. I slept better and I read more books than in the previous two years. I also took up running, which I enjoy far more than watching videos. My friendships improved too: meeting people in person is not as convenient as sending messages, but it is much more worthwhile. Now I use social media again, but I spend nowhere near as much time on it.

2.title: Two jobs, one choice
2.brief: You have two job offers. Write an email to a friend comparing them and asking for advice.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo comparando dos ofertas de trabajo y pidiéndole consejo.
criteria: Six comparisons, including “the same as” or “similar to”.
One gerund phrase as subject (Working from home sounds…).
Ask for advice with a question at the end.
2.model:
Hi Sebas,

I need your advice! I've got two job offers. The first is at a big bank. The salary is higher and the office is closer to my flat, but I would work longer hours than now. The second is at a small startup. The pay is lower, but it is far more flexible: working from home three days a week sounds amazing. The team is younger and the work seems more creative. Both jobs are similar to my current one, but the startup offers more training. On the other hand, the bank is more stable than a startup, and I'm worried about that. Taking a risk is not easy at my age! Which one would you choose?

Talk soon,
Diana

2.title: Getting to school
2.brief: Write a short report comparing three ways of getting to school or work. Use comparisons with adjectives, nouns and verbs, and finish with a recommendation.
2.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve que compare tres formas de ir al colegio o al trabajo y termina con una recomendación.
criteria: At least five comparisons with adjectives, nouns or verbs (more convenient, fewer lanes, spend less time).
At least two gerund phrases as subject (Travelling by bus is…).
Clear headings and one of these: “worthwhile”, “nowhere near” or “by far”.
2.model:
Report: how students travel to school

Introduction
This report compares the three most common ways to get to our school: the bus, cycling and walking.

Findings
Travelling by bus is far more convenient on rainy days, but it is also more expensive. A monthly ticket costs 28 euros, whereas cycling is almost free. Many students say that the bus is too crowded in the morning. Cyclists also arrive earlier than bus passengers, because they spend less time waiting. However, there are fewer safe cycle lanes near the school than there are bus stops. Walking is the healthiest option, although it is nowhere near as fast as the others.

Recommendation
I recommend building more cycle lanes and offering cheaper bus tickets to students. Cycling to school is worthwhile because students save money and get more exercise.

2.title: Two phones, one winner
2.brief: Write a review comparing two products you have used, such as phones, headphones or trainers, and say which one you recommend.
2.briefEs: Escribe una reseña que compare dos productos que hayas usado y di cuál recomiendas.
criteria: At least four comparisons, including one with a noun (fewer apps) and one with a verb (works more slowly).
At least two gerund phrases as subject.
Use “time-consuming” or “worthwhile” and “by far”.
2.model:
Two phones, one winner

I have used the Nova 5 and the Zeta Lite for a month, and the Zeta Lite is the better choice. It costs 40 euros less, and its battery lasts much longer. Charging the Nova 5 is more time-consuming because the cable is slow. On the other hand, the Nova 5 has a better camera and takes sharper photos. The Zeta Lite has fewer apps installed, so it has more free memory. Both phones are similar in size, but the Nova 5 works more slowly when I open several apps. Choosing a phone is difficult, but for students on a budget the Zeta Lite is by far the most worthwhile option.

2.title: Madrid or Valencia?
2.brief: You must choose between two cities to study in. Write an email to a friend comparing them and asking two questions at the end.
2.briefEs: Debes elegir entre dos ciudades para estudiar. Escribe un correo a una amiga comparándolas y termina con dos preguntas.
criteria: At least five comparisons, including one with a noun (more universities) and one with a past participle (less crowded).
One gerund phrase as subject (Moving away from home is…).
End with two questions asking for opinions.
2.model:
Hi Ainhoa,

I need your help with a big decision. I have to choose between studying in Madrid or in Valencia. Madrid is much bigger than Valencia, so there are more universities and more job opportunities. However, living there is far more expensive. A small room costs about 450 euros a month, whereas in Valencia it costs around 300. Valencia is also less crowded, and it has more sunshine. On the other hand, Madrid's metro is more efficient than the buses in Valencia. Moving away from home is scary, but I think it will be worthwhile. Have you ever lived in either city? Which one would you choose?

Lots of love,
Paula

2.title: Cooking at home or eating out?
2.brief: Is cooking at home better than eating out? Write an opinion essay that compares both options and gives your conclusion.
2.briefEs: ¿Es mejor cocinar en casa que comer fuera? Escribe un ensayo de opinión que compare ambas opciones y concluya.
criteria: At least two gerund phrases as subject with a singular verb.
At least five comparisons with adjectives, nouns and verbs (cheaper than, fewer burgers, as much as).
Use “to take up”, “advantage” and “worthwhile”.
2.model:
Is cooking at home better than eating out?

Many young people think that eating out is more fun, but I disagree. Cooking at home is cheaper than going to restaurants, and it is usually healthier too. A pizza in my town costs about 12 euros, whereas I can make one at home for less than four. Preparing a meal can be time-consuming, but it is also a good way to relax after school. I have learned a lot about food since I took up cooking last year, and I eat far fewer burgers than before. Learning to cook is also a skill that you will use all your life. Of course, restaurants are more convenient when you are tired, and they have more variety. However, the advantages of cooking at home are much greater. In the long run, it is the more worthwhile choice.

2.title: Learning the guitar
2.brief: Write an article comparing three ways of learning a skill (an instrument, a sport or a language). Say which one worked best for you.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo que compare tres formas de aprender una habilidad y di cuál te funcionó mejor.
criteria: At least three gerund phrases as subject (Learning…, Using…, Watching…).
At least five comparisons with adjectives, nouns or verbs.
Use “drawback”, “to take up” and “nowhere near” or “by far”.
2.model:
Learning the guitar: teacher, app or videos?

Learning an instrument is not easy, so choosing the right method matters. A private teacher is by far the most effective option because he or she corrects your mistakes immediately. However, lessons are expensive, and they cost more than twice as much as an app subscription. Using an app is cheaper and more flexible. You can practise on the bus, but you get less feedback than with a teacher. Watching free videos is the cheapest choice of all. The main drawback is that beginners often copy bad habits without noticing. I took up the guitar two years ago, and I combined a monthly lesson with an app. That mix is nowhere near as expensive as weekly lessons, and I have made real progress. It was a worthwhile decision.

2.title: Gym or running?
2.brief: Write a chat between two friends who disagree about how to exercise. They compare the two options in short messages.
2.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos que no coinciden sobre cómo hacer ejercicio y comparan las dos opciones en mensajes cortos.
criteria: At least three comparisons (cheaper than, more crowded than, fewer… than).
At least one gerund phrase as subject.
Between six and eight short lines, alternating speakers.
2.model:
Nico: Are you going to the gym or running today?
Elena: Running is cheaper than the gym, so I prefer that.
Nico: But exercising indoors is more comfortable when it rains.
Elena: True, but the gym is more crowded than the park, and I have fewer free hours than you.
Nico: OK. Running together is more fun anyway. Shall we go at six?
Elena: Perfect!

3.title: A favour from a colleague
3.brief: You need a colleague to cover your work for two days. Write a polite email asking for help and explaining the situation.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo cortés pidiendo a un colega que cubra tu trabajo por dos días.
criteria: Three different request forms: Would you mind + -ing, I was wondering if, Would it be possible to…
One indirect question (Do you know whether…).
Use “to be tied up”, “appreciate” or “by any chance”.
3.model:
Hi Marcela,

I hope you're well. I'm writing because I have a family emergency and I need to travel to Pasto on Thursday and Friday. I was wondering if you could take care of my clients for those two days. Would you mind answering my emails and checking the orders? I know you're tied up with the new campaign, so please tell me if it's too much. Would it be possible to have a quick meeting tomorrow so I can explain everything? I'd also like to know whether you are free on Monday morning, by any chance, so I can thank you with a coffee. I really appreciate your help.

Best,
Óscar

3.title: Asking for information
3.brief: Write a formal email to a university or language school asking about a course. Use indirect questions throughout.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal a una universidad pidiendo información sobre un curso con preguntas indirectas.
criteria: Five indirect questions with statement word order.
Use “whether” in at least one question.
Formal register: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam, Yours faithfully.
3.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am interested in the Advanced English Writing course advertised on your website, and I would be grateful if you could send me some further information. Firstly, could you tell me when the next course starts? I would also like to know how many students there are in each group. I was wondering whether the classes are offered in the evening, as I work during the day. In addition, could you let me know if there is a placement test and how much it costs? Finally, I would appreciate it if you could tell me whether a certificate is awarded at the end of the course.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Andrea Salazar

3.title: Notes for a new neighbour
3.brief: A new family has moved in next door. Write a friendly note introducing yourself and making two requests politely.
3.briefEs: Escribe una nota amable a los vecinos nuevos presentándote y haciéndoles dos peticiones.
criteria: Use a request with an if-clause (I'd be grateful if you could…).
Use “Would you mind + -ing” once.
Offer help with “Don’t hesitate to…”.
3.model:
Dear neighbours,

Welcome to the building! My name is Ricardo and I live in 501, just above you. I hope you are settling in well. I have a small favour to ask. I work night shifts, so I sleep in the mornings. I'd be grateful if you could keep the noise down before 11 a.m., especially on weekdays. Also, would you mind not leaving bags of rubbish in the corridor? The building has a special area downstairs. I know moving house is stressful, so if you need anything, like a drill or a ladder, don't hesitate to knock on my door. I'm happy to give you a hand.

Best wishes,
Ricardo

3.title: Borrowing notes
3.brief: Write a chat between two classmates. One asks for notes and help with homework, using polite requests and indirect questions.
3.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos compañeros: uno pide apuntes y ayuda con los deberes usando peticiones corteses y preguntas indirectas.
criteria: At least three different request forms (Could you…, Do you mind if…, Would you mind + -ing, I was wondering if…).
At least one indirect question with if or whether.
One polite softener such as “I’m afraid” or “by any chance”.
3.model:
Ana: Hi Iván! Could you possibly send me your notes from Monday?
Iván: Sure. Do you mind if I send them tonight?
Ana: Not at all. I was wondering if you could also explain the last exercise.
Iván: Of course. Would you mind meeting me at the library at four?
Ana: Perfect. Do you know whether it's open today?
Iván: I'm afraid I don't. I'll check and let you know.

3.title: Changing a hotel booking
3.brief: Write a formal email to a hotel asking to change the dates of your booking. Use polite requests and indirect questions to ask about prices and facilities.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal a un hotel pidiendo cambiar las fechas de tu reserva, con peticiones corteses y preguntas indirectas sobre precios e instalaciones.
criteria: At least three different request forms (Would it be possible to…, Would you mind + -ing, I would be grateful if…).
At least two indirect questions with if or whether, in statement word order.
Formal register: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam and Yours faithfully.
3.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I have a reservation at your hotel for a double room from 14 to 17 July, under the name Hartmann. Unfortunately, my plans have changed, and I would be grateful if you could move my booking to 21 to 24 July. Would it be possible to keep the same room price? I was also wondering whether breakfast is still included, as it was not clear in my confirmation email. In addition, could you tell me if there is a car park and how much it costs per night? Finally, would you mind sending me written confirmation of the new dates? I am travelling with my elderly parents, so I would appreciate an early reply. I apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your help.

Yours faithfully,
Katrin Hartmann

3.title: Before I arrive
3.brief: You are going to stay with a host family. Write an email asking about the house, the food and the area with indirect questions.
3.briefEs: Vas a alojarte con una familia anfitriona. Escribe un correo preguntando por la casa, la comida y la zona con preguntas indirectas.
criteria: At least four indirect questions with statement word order (Could you tell me what time…).
At least one “Would you mind + -ing”.
Polite opening and closing (Dear…, Thank you…, Best wishes).
3.model:
Dear Mrs Evans,

Thank you for welcoming me into your home this summer! I'm really looking forward to meeting you all. I have a few questions before I arrive. Could you tell me what time dinner is usually served? I wonder whether I should bring a towel or if you have one for me. Do you know how far your house is from the language school? I'd also like to know if there's a washing machine I can use. Would you mind telling me what your children like doing? I'd love to bring them a small present from Ecuador. Thank you so much for your help.

Best wishes,
Juan

3.title: An extension for my project
3.brief: You were ill and cannot finish a school project on time. Write a polite email to your teacher asking for more time and for some information.
3.briefEs: Has estado enfermo y no puedes terminar un trabajo a tiempo. Escribe un correo cortés a tu profesor pidiendo más plazo e información.
criteria: At least three different request forms.
At least two indirect questions with if or whether.
Use “I’m afraid” and “appreciate”.
3.model:
Dear Mr Alvarado,

I am writing to ask for a favour. I am afraid I will not be able to hand in my history project on Friday, because I was ill for most of this week. Would it be possible to have an extension until next Tuesday? I would be very grateful if you could also let me know whether I need to give you a doctor's note. I have already finished the research, so I only need to write the conclusion. Would you mind telling me if the presentation date will change too? I understand that you are very busy, and I really appreciate your help.

Kind regards,
Martina Rojas

3.title: Help with a trip to Lisbon
3.brief: Write a post for a travel forum asking for advice about a trip. Use indirect questions and polite requests.
3.briefEs: Escribe un post para un foro de viajes pidiendo consejo sobre un viaje, con preguntas indirectas y peticiones corteses.
criteria: At least four indirect questions with statement word order, one of them with whether.
At least two different request forms (Would you mind…, I was wondering if…).
Use “I’m afraid” or “by any chance”.
3.model:
Hello everyone,

I'm travelling to Lisbon with two friends next month, and I have a few questions. Could anybody tell me which neighbourhood is best for young people? Does anyone know whether the metro runs all night? I was wondering if it's possible to buy a single ticket for trams and buses. We're also tied up with exams until the 20th, so I can't plan everything alone. Would you mind sharing your favourite cheap restaurants? Do you happen to know how much a taxi from the airport costs? I'm afraid my Portuguese is terrible, so any tips about useful phrases would be great. Any advice would be really appreciated. Thank you in advance!

Hanna

3.title: Lost luggage
3.brief: Your suitcase did not arrive after a flight. Write a formal letter of complaint to the airline, asking politely for information and compensation.
3.briefEs: Tu maleta no llegó tras un vuelo. Escribe una carta formal de queja a la aerolínea pidiendo cortésmente información y compensación.
criteria: At least three different request forms (I would appreciate it if…, Could you let me know…, Would you mind + -ing).
At least two indirect questions with whether, if or a wh-word.
Formal register: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam and Yours faithfully.
3.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about my suitcase, which did not arrive on flight AV204 from Bogotá to Madrid on 3 August. Since then, nobody has been able to tell me where it is. I would appreciate it if you could trace it as soon as possible. Could you let me know whether it is still in Colombia or if it has been sent to another airport? I would also be grateful if you could tell me what compensation I can expect. The suitcase contained my school books, so I had to buy new ones for 85 euros. Would you mind refunding this amount? I am staying with my aunt in Madrid, and I would be happy to give you her address and phone number. I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Camila Torres

4.title: A journey that went wrong
4.brief: Write a story about a journey that went wrong. Use the past continuous for background, the simple past for events and the past perfect for earlier events.
4.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre un viaje que salió mal usando pasado continuo, pasado simple y pasado perfecto.
criteria: Two past continuous verbs for background.
Three past perfect verbs (had left, had forgotten).
Use “by the time”, “eventually” and “delay” or “to break down”.
4.model: It was raining heavily when we left Bogotá for the coast. My brother was driving and I was choosing the music. After three hours, the car broke down in the middle of nowhere. We realised that my brother had forgotten to check the oil before the trip. While we were waiting for help, I discovered that I had left my phone charger at home. By the time a mechanic arrived, it was dark and we were starving. The repair took four more hours. Meanwhile, we ate the sandwiches our mother had prepared. Eventually, we arrived at the hotel at two in the morning, but the receptionist had given our room to someone else! It was a trip we will never forget.

4.title: Witness statement
4.brief: You saw an accident or a robbery. Write a witness statement for the police describing what happened in order.
4.briefEs: Escribe una declaración como testigo para la policía describiendo lo que pasó.
criteria: Past continuous for what people were doing when it happened.
Two past perfect verbs to show earlier actions.
Formal, clear sequence: first, then, by the time.
4.model:
Statement of: Carolina Mejía
On Tuesday, 14 March, at about 6:30 p.m., I was standing at the bus stop on Carrera Séptima. It was getting dark and many people were walking home. A man in a grey jacket was looking at the shop windows. Suddenly, he ran into the phone shop and grabbed two phones from the counter. I noticed that he had parked a motorbike outside, because the engine was still running. The shop assistant shouted, but by the time she reached the door, the man had already left. I had seen the motorbike before, at around six o'clock, so I think he had been watching the shop. I wrote down part of the number plate: XYZ 4.

4.title: Why I was late
4.brief: You arrived very late for an important meeting. Write an email to apologise and explain what had happened.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal disculpándote por llegar tarde y explicando lo que había pasado.
criteria: Use the past perfect to explain earlier causes.
Use “while” or “when” with past continuous.
Use a formal apology: I would like to apologise for…
4.model:
Dear Mr. Castro,

I would like to apologise for arriving forty minutes late to this morning's meeting. I had left home with plenty of time, but while I was crossing the city, there was a serious accident on the Avenida Boyacá. The police had closed two lanes, so traffic was barely moving. When I tried to call you, I realised that my phone had died, because I had forgotten to charge it the night before. By the time I arrived, you had already presented the main points. I understand this caused a delay, and I would be happy to meet again tomorrow to go over anything I missed.

Kind regards,
Natalia Pérez

4.title: Lost at the festival
4.brief: Write a story about something that went wrong at a festival, concert or party. Use the past continuous for the background, the simple past for events and the past perfect for earlier actions.
4.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre algo que salió mal en un festival, concierto o fiesta, con pasado continuo, pasado simple y pasado perfecto.
criteria: At least three past continuous verbs for background.
At least three past perfect verbs for earlier actions.
Use “by the time”, “meanwhile” and “eventually”.
4.model: It was a hot Saturday afternoon, and we were queuing for the gates of the music festival in Valencia. My friend Irene was telling a joke when I realised that my phone was not in my pocket. I had put it in my bag that morning, but the bag was now open. While I was searching for it, the doors opened and the crowd pushed us inside. By the time we reached the stage, the first band had already started playing. I felt terrible, because all my tickets and photos were on that phone. Meanwhile, Irene was asking people near us if they had seen it. Eventually, a security guard called my name. A girl had found the phone on the grass and had handed it in. I almost cried with joy.

4.title: You won't believe it!
4.brief: Write an email to a friend about a surprise party that did not go as planned. Explain what was happening and what had happened before.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre una fiesta sorpresa que no salió como se esperaba: qué estaba pasando y qué había ocurrido antes.
criteria: At least three past continuous verbs.
At least three past perfect verbs.
Use “by the time” and “in the end”.
4.model:
Hi Gabi,

You won't believe what happened on Saturday! We were preparing a surprise party for Toni when he walked in an hour early. His mum had told him the wrong time, so nobody was ready. I was blowing up balloons while my cousin was hanging the banner, and the cake was still in the oven. Toni looked at us and started laughing. By the time the guests arrived, he had already eaten half of the cake! In the end, it was a great evening because everybody had brought music and snacks. I'm sorry you weren't there. Next time, I'll tell you the real time!

Speak soon,
David

4.title: Fire alarm at Riverside School
4.brief: Write a short news article for a school website about an unexpected event. Say what was happening, what interrupted it and what had caused it.
4.briefEs: Escribe una noticia breve para la web del colegio sobre un suceso inesperado: qué ocurría, qué lo interrumpió y qué lo había causado.
criteria: At least three past continuous verbs for the background.
At least two past perfect verbs.
Use “to go off”, “delay” and “eventually”.
4.model:
Fire alarm interrupts exams at Riverside School

Yesterday morning, about 200 students were sitting their maths exams when the fire alarm went off. The teachers had checked the building the day before, so nobody expected a problem. Students left calmly while the head teacher was calling the fire brigade. By the time the firefighters arrived, everybody had gathered on the football pitch. Meanwhile, caretaker Mr Bell was looking into the cause. He discovered that a pupil had burnt toast in the canteen kitchen during a cooking class. Nobody was hurt, but the exams suffered a long delay. Eventually, the students returned to their classrooms at noon. The school has promised to review its safety procedures.

4.title: A delayed train
4.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint about a delayed journey that made you miss something important. Explain the sequence of events in order.
4.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja sobre un viaje retrasado que te hizo perder algo importante, explicando la secuencia de hechos.
criteria: At least two past continuous verbs (While we were waiting…).
At least three past perfect verbs to explain earlier causes.
Formal complaint language: I am writing to complain, I would be grateful if…, Yours faithfully.
4.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the 8.15 train from Leeds to London on Monday 12 May. When I arrived at the station, the platform was already crowded because the previous train had been cancelled. While we were waiting, nobody made an announcement, so we did not know what was happening. The train eventually left forty minutes late. By the time I reached London, my job interview had already finished and the company had given the position to another candidate. I had left home at six to arrive early, so the delay was very frustrating. A member of staff had promised me a refund of the ticket, but I have not received it. I would be grateful if you could look into this matter and refund my ticket of 47 pounds.

Yours faithfully,
Peter Moore

4.title: I missed the bus
4.brief: Write a chat in which a friend explains why he or she did not arrive at school. Use the past continuous, the simple past and the past perfect.
4.briefEs: Escribe un chat en el que un amigo explica por qué no llegó al colegio, con pasado continuo, pasado simple y pasado perfecto.
criteria: At least two past continuous verbs.
At least one past perfect verb.
Use “by the time” and “eventually”.
4.model:
Sam: Where were you this morning?
Nora: I was running to the bus stop when I tripped over a dog!
Sam: Oh no! Were you OK?
Nora: Yes, but by the time I stood up, the bus had left.
Sam: So how did you get to school?
Nora: Eventually, my neighbour was driving past and gave me a lift.

4.title: A holiday disaster
4.brief: Write a forum post about a travel problem you or your family had. Describe the background, the events and what had happened before.
4.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro sobre un problema de viaje que tuviste con tu familia: contexto, hechos y lo que había pasado antes.
criteria: At least three past continuous verbs.
At least three past perfect verbs.
Use “meanwhile”, “in the meantime” and “by the time”.
4.model:
Hello everyone,

Last summer, my family and I were queuing to board a ferry to Mallorca when my dad realised that he had left our passports in the taxi. My mum was shouting at him while my little sister was crying. Meanwhile, I ran to the taxi rank, but the driver had already left. In the meantime, a kind port employee was looking into the problem on his computer. By the time he found the taxi company, the ferry had gone without us. Eventually, the driver brought the passports back and we took the next boat at midnight. It was an awful day, but we still laugh about it. Has anything similar ever happened to you?

Elena

5.title: Customs in my country
5.brief: Write an article for foreign visitors explaining some customs in Colombia: what is expected, acceptable or not acceptable.
5.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para visitantes extranjeros sobre costumbres colombianas: lo esperado y lo inaceptable.
criteria: Use four expressions: it’s the custom to, be (not) supposed to, be expected to, it’s (not) acceptable to.
Two noun phrases with relative clauses (People who visit…, A guest who arrives…).
Use “etiquette” and “to frown on”.
5.model: If you visit Colombia, some local etiquette will help you fit in. When you meet someone, it's the custom to greet them with a handshake or, between women and between friends, a kiss on the cheek. People who are invited to dinner are expected to arrive a little late — arriving exactly on time is not common! It's acceptable to bring a small gift, like wine or dessert. At work, you are supposed to greet everyone in the office when you arrive, not only your boss. Colombians frown on people who don't say "buenos días". A visitor who refuses a cup of coffee may seem rude, so accept at least one. Finally, it's not acceptable to talk about drugs or violence as a joke.

5.title: Advice for an exchange student
5.brief: An exchange student is coming to your city. Write an email explaining the unwritten rules at your school or university.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un estudiante de intercambio explicando las reglas no escritas de tu universidad.
criteria: Three expressions of expectation (supposed to, expected to, acceptable).
Two noun phrases containing relative clauses.
Use “unwritten rule” or “to get away with”.
5.model:
Hi Lukas,

I'm glad you're coming to study here! Let me tell you some unwritten rules. Students who arrive late are not usually punished, but you're expected to apologise to the professor. You're supposed to call professors "profe", which is friendly but respectful. It's acceptable to eat in class, but not hot food! The library is a place where silence is really important, and you can't get away with talking on the phone. Another unwritten rule: the person who has a birthday is expected to bring a cake for the group. Finally, it's the custom to go out for empanadas after exams.

See you soon!
Marta

5.title: A social mistake
5.brief: Write about a time when you or someone you know broke a social rule (in another country or at a family event). Explain what happened and what the rule is.
5.briefEs: Escribe sobre una vez en que tú u otra persona rompió una norma social, y explica cuál es la norma.
criteria: Explain the rule with “be (not) supposed to” or “it’s (not) the custom to”.
Two noun phrases with relative clauses.
Use “to offend”, “appropriate” or “norm”.
5.model: When I first visited Japan, I made a mistake that I still remember. At a restaurant, I left a tip on the table for the waiter who had served us. A few minutes later, he ran after me in the street to return the money! I felt embarrassed. I learned that in Japan you are not supposed to tip; it can even offend people. The norm there is that good service is part of the job. Back home in Colombia, it's the custom to leave ten percent, so it's appropriate for me. The thing I learned from that trip is simple: people who travel should read about local customs before they go.

5.title: Eating with a Mexican family
5.brief: Write an article for visitors about the etiquette of eating at a family home in a country you know. Say what is the custom, expected and acceptable.
5.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para visitantes sobre la etiqueta al comer en casa de una familia de un país que conozcas: costumbres, expectativas y lo aceptable.
criteria: At least four expressions of expectation: it’s the custom to, be supposed to, be expected to, it’s acceptable to.
At least two noun phrases with relative clauses (Guests who…, The kind of behaviour that…).
Use “etiquette” and “to frown on” or “norm”.
5.model:
Eating with a Mexican family: what to expect

If you are invited to a Mexican home for lunch, it helps to know some etiquette. Guests who arrive on time may find the family still cooking, so it's the custom to arrive about fifteen minutes late. You are not supposed to start eating until the host invites everybody to begin. It is acceptable to ask for more food, and people who finish everything on the plate are seen as polite. Visitors are expected to try every dish, even a very spicy one. The kind of behaviour that most families frown on is leaving the table early, so stay for the long conversation after the meal. Finally, remember to thank the cook. It is the norm to say it more than once!

5.title: Your first week at work in London
5.brief: A friend is starting work experience abroad. Write an email explaining the unwritten rules of the workplace.
5.briefEs: Un amigo empieza unas prácticas en el extranjero. Escribe un correo explicándole las reglas no escritas del lugar de trabajo.
criteria: At least three expressions of expectation (supposed to, expected to, acceptable, the custom).
At least two noun phrases with relative clauses.
Use “unwritten rule” or “etiquette”.
5.model:
Hi Elsa,

Congratulations on your work experience in London! I did the same thing last year, so here are some unwritten rules. The people who work there are friendly, but they expect you to be punctual. You're supposed to arrive five minutes early, not late. It's the custom to say good morning to everyone, and it's acceptable to call your manager by her first name. Lunch is short, and you're not supposed to eat at your desk. Colleagues who ask how you are don't want a long answer, so just say fine, thanks! One thing that might surprise you is that people often say sorry for everything. Enjoy it, and send me a message when you arrive.

Best,
Owen

5.title: What is normal on the bus?
5.brief: You are new in a city. Write a forum post asking about the unwritten rules of public transport and explaining what is different in your country.
5.briefEs: Eres nuevo en una ciudad. Escribe un post de foro preguntando por las reglas no escritas del transporte público y explicando qué es distinto en tu país.
criteria: At least three expressions of expectation.
At least two noun phrases with relative clauses.
Use “unwritten rule”, “norm” and “to offend”.
5.model:
Hello everyone,

I'm a new student in Lima, and I'm trying to understand the unwritten rules on public transport. In my country, people who sit near the door are expected to give their seat to older passengers. Is it the same here? I've also noticed that the passengers who talk loudly on the phone get angry looks, so I think it isn't acceptable. Another thing I can't work out is whether you're supposed to say hello to the driver. Back home, it's the custom to greet him, but nobody does it here. Could somebody explain what the norms are? I don't want to offend anyone. Thanks a lot!

Jonas

5.title: Is it acceptable to arrive late?
5.brief: Is it acceptable to arrive late to a party? Write an opinion essay about punctuality and social expectations.
5.briefEs: ¿Es aceptable llegar tarde a una fiesta? Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre la puntualidad y las expectativas sociales.
criteria: At least three expectation structures (acceptable, supposed to, expected to…).
At least three noun phrases with relative clauses (guests who…, The kind of guest that…).
Use “norm” and “unwritten rule”.
5.model:
Is it acceptable to arrive late to a party?

In many countries, arriving late to a party is the norm. In Argentina, for example, guests who arrive on time are sometimes seen as strange, because the hosts are not ready. In my opinion, a short delay of fifteen or twenty minutes is perfectly acceptable. However, people who arrive two hours late without a message are being rude. The thing that matters most is respect. If you are supposed to meet somebody at a restaurant, you are expected to be on time, because the staff are waiting. At a house party, the rules are different. The kind of guest that every host likes is the one who brings a small gift and helps to clear up. That is the unwritten rule I follow.

5.title: Behaviour in the study room
5.brief: Write a short report on behaviour in a shared place at your school (library, canteen, study room). Describe the unwritten rules and recommend changes.
5.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve sobre el comportamiento en un lugar compartido de tu colegio, describiendo las reglas no escritas y recomendando cambios.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations.
At least three expectation structures (supposed to, not acceptable, expected to, frowned on).
At least two noun phrases with relative clauses.
5.model:
Report: behaviour in the school study room

Introduction
This report describes the unwritten rules in our study room and recommends some changes.

Findings
Students who use the room are supposed to keep silent, but many people talk on the phone. It is not acceptable to leave bags on empty chairs during exams, yet this is a common habit. Most students who were interviewed said that eating is frowned on, although it still happens. The kind of noise that bothers people most is music from headphones.

Recommendations
We should put up clear signs. Students are expected to follow them, and the librarian should be allowed to ask people to leave.

5.title: What should I wear?
5.brief: Write a chat between two friends. One asks what is expected at a family event, and the other explains the customs.
5.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos: uno pregunta qué se espera en un evento familiar y el otro explica las costumbres.
criteria: At least three expectation expressions (supposed to, expected to, acceptable, the custom).
Use “frowned on” and “unwritten rule”.
Between four and six messages, alternating speakers.
5.model:
Inés: I'm going to my cousin's wedding. What am I supposed to wear?
Hugo: Guests are expected to dress smartly, so no jeans.
Inés: Is it acceptable to wear white?
Hugo: No, that's frowned on. It's the custom to leave white for the bride. Also, there's an unwritten rule: you shouldn't leave before the first dance.
Inés: Thanks! I'll wear blue and stay late.

6.title: A complaint about a faulty product
6.brief: Write a complaint email to an online shop about a product that arrived damaged or stopped working.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo de reclamo a una tienda en línea sobre un producto que llegó dañado o dejó de funcionar.
criteria: Three past participles as adjectives (cracked, scratched, broken).
Two “need + gerund / passive infinitive” structures.
Use “keep + gerund”, “warranty” and “to replace”.
6.model:
Dear Customer Service,

I am writing to complain about the laptop I ordered from your website on 2 May (order number 45821). When it arrived, the box was damaged and the screen was cracked in one corner. The keyboard is also scratched. In addition, the laptop keeps switching off after ten minutes, so I cannot use it for work. It clearly needs to be repaired, or, better, it needs replacing. As the laptop is still under warranty, I would like you to replace it with a new one or give me a full refund. I have attached photos of the damage. I hope you can solve this problem quickly.

Yours faithfully,
Jorge Ramírez

6.title: Things that need fixing
6.brief: You are moving out of a rented flat. Write a note to the landlord listing problems in the flat and what each one needs.
6.briefEs: Escribe una nota al arrendador con los problemas del apartamento y lo que necesita cada uno.
criteria: Describe five problems with participles or nouns (a leak, a stain, loose, dented).
Use “need + -ing” and “need to be + past participle”.
Use “to wear out” or “faulty”.
6.model:
Dear Mr. Suárez,

Before I move out, I would like to tell you about some problems in the flat. There is a leak under the kitchen sink, so the pipe needs to be repaired. The bathroom door handle is loose and it needs tightening. There is a big stain on the living room carpet; I think it needs cleaning by a professional. The fridge door is dented and the light inside is faulty. Finally, the sofa is worn out and it needs to be replaced soon. The shower keeps dripping, too. I'm sorry I couldn't fix these things myself.

Best regards,
Valentina

6.title: My worst repair experience
6.brief: Tell the story of something that broke and the problems you had getting it fixed.
6.briefEs: Cuenta la historia de algo que se dañó y los problemas que tuviste para arreglarlo.
criteria: Use “keep + gerund” twice.
Use “need + passive infinitive” once.
Three words for damage (cracked, leak, faulty, loose…).
6.model: Last year my washing machine started making a strange noise. Then it kept stopping in the middle of every wash, and water kept leaking onto the floor. I called a technician, who said that one part was faulty and needed to be replaced. He took the old part and promised to come back in two days. He didn't come back for three weeks! Meanwhile, I had to wash my clothes by hand. When he finally returned, he installed the new part, but the door was loose and the glass was cracked. I asked him to fix it, but he said it wasn't his job. In the end, I bought a new machine. Now I always ask for a warranty.

6.title: Hotel Mirador
6.brief: Write a negative review of a hotel, hostel or flat you stayed in. Describe the faults with participles and nouns and say what each one needs.
6.briefEs: Escribe una reseña negativa de un hotel o alojamiento describiendo los defectos con participios y sustantivos y diciendo qué necesita cada uno.
criteria: At least three faults described with past participles or problem nouns (stained, loose, a leak).
One “need + -ing” and one “need to be + past participle”.
Use “keep + -ing” and “to fix”.
6.model:
Hotel Mirador: not worth the price

I stayed at this hotel for three nights in Seville, and the experience was disappointing. The room looked nice in the photos, but in real life the carpet was stained and the wardrobe door was loose. The bathroom had a leak under the sink, so the floor was always wet. The air conditioning kept making a loud noise, and it clearly needs replacing. I asked reception to fix it, but nobody came. On the positive side, the breakfast was delicious and the staff were friendly. However, a hotel that charges 95 euros a night needs to be properly maintained. I would not stay there again.

6.title: Before the landlord comes
6.brief: Write an email to a flatmate listing the things in your flat that need fixing or cleaning before an inspection. Share the jobs between you.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un compañero de piso con lo que hay que arreglar o limpiar antes de una inspección, repartiendo las tareas.
criteria: At least four faults described with participles or problem nouns (scratched, a stain, cracked, broken).
At least two “need” structures, one of them with a passive infinitive.
Use “keep + -ing” once.
6.model:
Hi Jess,

The landlord is coming on Friday to inspect the flat, so we need to sort a few things out. First, the bathroom tap keeps dripping, and it needs fixing. The sofa is badly scratched, but we can cover it with a blanket. There's also a stain on the kitchen wall that needs cleaning. I'll do that tomorrow. Could you take the broken lamp to the repair shop? I think the cable needs to be replaced. The living room window is cracked in one corner too, but I'm going to tell him about it myself. If we're honest, he can't blame us because it was already damaged when we moved in. Thanks for your help!

Zoe

6.title: My phone keeps freezing
6.brief: Write a chat between two friends about a phone that has several problems. They decide whether to repair or replace it.
6.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos sobre un móvil con varios problemas: deciden si repararlo o cambiarlo.
criteria: At least three problems described (cracked, faulty, worn out, keeps freezing).
At least two “need” structures (needs replacing, needs to be repaired).
Mention “warranty” and use “keep + -ing” once.
6.model:
Dani: My phone keeps freezing and the screen is cracked.
Lucas: It definitely needs to be repaired. Is it still under warranty?
Dani: No, the warranty ended last month.
Lucas: Then it needs replacing.
Dani: Ugh. The battery is worn out as well, and it keeps switching off.
Lucas: Mine was faulty too, so I bought a new one.

6.title: Problems in Classroom 3
6.brief: Write a formal letter of complaint to a school or language academy about the poor condition of a classroom. Describe the faults and say what they need.
6.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal de queja a un colegio o academia sobre el mal estado de un aula, describiendo los fallos y lo que necesitan.
criteria: At least four faults described with participles or problem nouns.
At least two “need” structures, one with a passive infinitive.
Use “keep + -ing” and a formal request (I would be grateful if…).
6.model:
Dear Mr Whitaker,

I am a student on the intermediate course at your language school, and I am writing to complain about the condition of Classroom 3. The projector is faulty and keeps switching off during lessons, so the teacher has to write everything on the board. The board itself is badly scratched and needs replacing. Several chairs are loose, and one of them was so damaged that a student almost fell. In addition, there is a leak in the ceiling, which needs to be repaired before winter. Our class pays 180 euros a month, and we believe that the equipment should be in good condition. I would be grateful if the projector could be replaced as soon as possible.

Yours sincerely,
Hannah Peters

6.title: The school sports hall
6.brief: Write a short report on the condition of a room or facility at your school. List the faults and recommend repairs.
6.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve sobre el estado de una instalación de tu colegio, con los fallos y las reparaciones que recomiendas.
criteria: At least four faults described with participles or problem nouns.
At least two “need” structures, one with a passive infinitive.
Headings: Introduction, Problems, Recommendations, and one use of “keep + -ing”.
6.model:
Report: the condition of the school sports hall

Introduction
This report describes the main problems in the sports hall after a visit on 10 March.

Problems
The floor is badly worn out near the basketball hoops, and one board is cracked. Two benches are broken. One window is loose and two are scratched. There is a leak above the changing rooms, and a stain on the ceiling is growing. The main lights keep flickering, which makes training difficult.

Recommendations
The floor needs to be repaired during the summer holidays. The benches need replacing, and the lights should be checked by an electrician. These repairs are urgent because 300 students use the hall every week.

6.title: Is it worth repairing?
6.brief: Write a forum post asking for advice about an old device that has several problems. Explain the faults and what they need, and ask whether it is worth repairing.
6.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro pidiendo consejo sobre un aparato viejo con varios problemas: explica los fallos y pregunta si merece la pena repararlo.
criteria: At least three problems described with participles or problem nouns (scratched, loose, worn out).
One “need to be + past participle” and one “keep + -ing”.
Use “warranty” and finish with a clear question.
6.model:
Hello everyone,

I need some advice. My laptop is three years old and it keeps shutting down without warning. I have already tried restarting it and cleaning the fans. The screen is slightly scratched and one key is loose, but the real problem is the battery, which is worn out. A technician says the whole battery needs to be replaced, and he wants 120 euros. A new laptop would cost about 500. The warranty ended last year, so I have to pay for everything. I use the laptop every day for school, so I can't live without it. Do you think it's worth fixing, or would it be better to buy a new one? Any ideas would help me a lot.

Thanks,
Marcos

7.title: Changes in my city
7.brief: Write an article for a local website about the changes that are being made in your city or neighbourhood, and their causes and effects.
7.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre los cambios que se están haciendo en tu ciudad, con causas y efectos.
criteria: Two passives in the present continuous (is being built) and two in the present perfect (has been opened).
Use due to, as a result of and thanks to.
Two infinitive clauses of purpose (in order to reduce…).
7.model: Our neighbourhood is changing fast. A new metro station is being built on Avenida 68, and several streets are being closed as a result of the work. In the last year, two parks have been renovated and a new library has been opened. Thanks to these projects, families have more places to spend time together. However, not all the effects are positive. Due to the construction, traffic has become terrible, and many small shops have lost customers. The city council has promised that the metro will be finished by 2027. In order to help local businesses, a special fund has been created. In my opinion, the changes are necessary, but they are being done too slowly.

7.title: An update for the team
7.brief: Write an email to your team explaining the status of a project: what is being done, what has been done and why.
7.briefEs: Escribe un correo al equipo explicando el estado de un proyecto: qué se está haciendo y qué se ha hecho.
criteria: Four passive forms in present continuous and present perfect.
Two infinitive phrases (to save time, in order to…).
Use “to be under way”, “ongoing” or “to carry out”.
7.model:
Hi everyone,

Here is a quick update on the website project. The new design has been approved by the director, and the photos have been uploaded. At the moment, the texts are being translated into English in order to reach more international clients. Some tests are being carried out by the IT team to check the speed of the site. Unfortunately, the launch has been delayed due to a problem with the payment system, but the solution is already under way. To save time, I suggest we meet for only fifteen minutes on Monday. The ongoing work should be finished by next Friday.

Thanks for your effort,
Pablo

7.title: A problem and its causes
7.brief: Choose an environmental or social problem in your country. Explain what is causing it and what is being done to solve it.
7.briefEs: Elige un problema ambiental o social y explica qué lo causa y qué se está haciendo para solucionarlo.
criteria: Use three prepositions of cause: due to, because of, as a result of.
Two passives in the present continuous or present perfect.
Use “to affect” and “consequence” correctly.
7.model: Deforestation in the Amazon is one of Colombia's most serious problems. Thousands of hectares have been lost in the last ten years, mainly due to cattle farming and illegal mining. As a result of this destruction, many animals have lost their habitat, and the climate in the whole region is being affected. One consequence is that rivers are becoming dry in some months. Fortunately, some things are being done. Protected areas have been created, and local communities are being paid to look after the forest. In my opinion, these programmes are a good start, but more needs to be done in order to stop the problem completely.

7.title: Our school is being renovated
7.brief: Write an article for your school magazine about a renovation or project in your school. Explain what is being done, what has been done, why, and what the effects are.
7.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para la revista del colegio sobre una reforma o proyecto: qué se está haciendo, qué se ha hecho, por qué y con qué efectos.
criteria: At least two passives in the present continuous (is being replaced) and two in the present perfect (has been installed).
Use due to, as a result of and thanks to.
At least two infinitive clauses of purpose (in order to make…, to save…).
7.model:
Our school is being renovated

This year, our school looks like a building site, but there are good reasons for it. The old science labs are being replaced by modern ones, and a new roof has been installed over the gym. Thanks to the renovation, students will have better facilities next September. Due to the noise, some lessons have been moved to the library. As a result of the works, the playground has been closed for two months, so we eat lunch in the corridors. The head teacher says that the work is being carried out in order to make the building safer and greener. Solar panels have already been fitted on the roof to save energy. In my opinion, we should be patient because the results will be worth it.

7.title: Roadworks on Mill Street
7.brief: You work for a town council. Write a formal email to residents explaining the roadworks in their street: what is being done, what has been done and why.
7.briefEs: Trabajas en un ayuntamiento. Escribe un correo formal a los vecinos explicando las obras de su calle: qué se está haciendo, qué se ha hecho y por qué.
criteria: At least two passives in the present continuous and two in the present perfect.
Use due to, as a result of and thanks to.
Formal register and one purpose clause with “in order to”.
7.model:
Dear residents,

We are writing to inform you about the work that is currently being carried out on Mill Street. The old water pipes are being replaced in order to prevent leaks. As a result of this work, parking has been suspended on both sides of the street, and the bus stop has been moved to the corner. Due to the heavy machinery, there may be some noise between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. The first section of the road has already been finished, thanks to the good weather. The council expects the work to be completed by the end of June. We apologise for any inconvenience and thank you for your patience.

Yours faithfully,
The Roads Department

7.title: Noise from the building site
7.brief: Write a formal letter complaining about building work near your home. Explain the effects on residents and what you would like to be done.
7.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal quejándote de unas obras cerca de tu casa: explica los efectos en los vecinos y qué te gustaría que se hiciera.
criteria: At least two passives in the present continuous and three in the present perfect.
Use due to, as a result of and because of.
One purpose clause with “in order to” and a formal request (I would be grateful if…).
7.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the building work that is being carried out next to my flat on Calle del Sol. Since the beginning of March, the street has been affected by constant noise from 7 a.m. As a result of the drilling, my little brother has not been able to study for his exams. Due to the dust, the windows of the whole building have been covered in dirt, and the entrance has been blocked twice by lorries. I understand that the work is being done in order to build new flats. However, because of the lack of planning, residents have not been informed about the schedule. I would be grateful if the working hours could be reduced and if the street could be cleaned every week.

Yours faithfully,
Alberto Navarro

7.title: The school recycling scheme
7.brief: Write a short report on the progress of a project at your school or in your town. Say what has been done, what is being done and what the consequences are.
7.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve sobre el progreso de un proyecto de tu colegio o ciudad: qué se ha hecho, qué se está haciendo y qué consecuencias tiene.
criteria: At least two passives in the present continuous and two in the present perfect.
Use thanks to, as a result of and due to.
At least two infinitive clauses of purpose and clear headings.
7.model:
Report: the school recycling scheme

Introduction
This report explains what has been done since the recycling scheme started in September.

Progress
Colour-coded bins have been placed in every classroom, and posters have been put up in the corridors. Thanks to the students' help, more than 400 kilos of paper have been collected. Plastic bottles are being sorted by the Year 9 class in order to save time for the cleaners. A competition is also being organised to encourage students to take part.

Consequences
As a result of the scheme, the school has reduced its rubbish by a third. Due to this success, the council has offered us a small grant.

7.title: Is the trip still on?
7.brief: Write a chat between two students who talk about the arrangements for a school trip. Use passives to say what has been done and what is being done.
7.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos estudiantes que hablan de los preparativos de un viaje escolar, con pasivas para lo hecho y lo que se está haciendo.
criteria: At least two passives in the present perfect and two in the present continuous.
Use “due to” and “thanks to”.
Between four and six messages, alternating speakers.
7.model:
Cris: Is the trip to Berlin still happening?
Adam: Yes! The hotel has been booked and the flights are being arranged.
Cris: Great. Has the schedule been finished?
Adam: Not yet. It's being checked by the teachers. Due to the strike, we might leave a day later.
Cris: OK. Thanks to you, I always know what's going on!

7.title: A new home for our club
7.brief: Write a blog post about a local club or team that is getting new facilities. Explain what is being built, what has been completed and why.
7.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre un club local que recibe nuevas instalaciones: qué se está construyendo, qué se ha terminado y por qué.
criteria: At least two passives in the present continuous and three in the present perfect.
Use thanks to, due to and as a result of.
At least one infinitive clause of purpose (in order to make space…).
7.model:
A new home for our club

Our local football club has been playing on a poor pitch for years, but things are changing. A new training ground is being built behind the sports centre, and the first stage has already been completed. Thanks to money from the town council, two modern pitches have been created. The old pitch has been repaired and will be used by the youngest teams. Due to the heavy rain in March, the opening has been delayed until September. Meanwhile, the old changing rooms are being demolished in order to make space for a gym. As a result of all these changes, many more children have joined the club this year. Volunteers are also being trained to help the younger players. It has been a long wait, but the club has finally got what it deserves.

8.title: City or countryside?
8.brief: Would you rather live in a big city or in the countryside? Give your preference and explain how you would make your life work there.
8.briefEs: ¿Preferirías vivir en la ciudad o en el campo? Da tu preferencia y explica cómo lo harías funcionar.
criteria: Use “would rather” and “would prefer” correctly (would rather + base form, would prefer + to).
Three “by + gerund” structures for methods.
Use “instead of” or “to be keen on”.
8.model: If I could choose, I would rather live in the countryside than in a big city. I would prefer to wake up to birds instead of car horns. Some people think rural life is boring, but I'm keen on nature and quiet places. Of course, I would need to work, so I would make money by working online as a translator. I would stay healthy by growing my own vegetables and by walking every day. The only problem would be loneliness, but I would solve it by joining community activities and by inviting friends from the city on weekends. I would rather have a simple life than a stressful one.

8.title: How to save money
8.brief: Write a blog post with practical tips for students who want to save money. Explain the method for each tip.
8.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog con consejos prácticos para que los estudiantes ahorren dinero.
criteria: Five “by + gerund” structures.
One sentence with “would rather” and one with “would prefer”.
Use “to cut down on” and “to work out”.
8.model: Being a student is expensive, but you can save a lot by making small changes. First, work out how much you spend every month by writing down every purchase for two weeks. You'll be surprised! Second, cut down on eating out. You can save up to 200,000 pesos a month by cooking at home and by taking lunch to university. Third, save on transport by cycling or walking short distances. Many students would rather take a taxi, but a bike is cheaper and healthier. Finally, avoid expensive subscriptions by sharing them with friends. Personally, I would prefer to have one streaming service than five that I never use. Saving gradually is better than not saving at all.

8.title: Choosing a holiday
8.brief: Your friend has suggested a beach holiday. Write an email saying you would prefer something different and explain how you could organise it.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo diciendo que preferirías otro tipo de vacaciones y explica cómo organizarlas.
criteria: Use would rather (not) and would prefer (not) to.
Two “by + gerund” structures.
One expression: to be worth it, means, method.
8.model:
Hi Juli,

Thanks for the idea of going to Santa Marta! But to be honest, I'd rather not spend another holiday on a hot beach. I'd prefer to do something more active this time. What about hiking in the Cocora Valley? I would rather sleep in a small cabin than in a big hotel. We could save money by sharing a room and by cooking our own meals. We can get there easily by taking a bus to Salento, then a jeep. I know it's colder, but I'm sure it'll be worth it. I'd prefer not to go in December because it's so crowded. What do you think?

Love,
Mafe

8.title: Loft or Tuscan house?
8.brief: Compare the loft and the Tuscan house in Unit 8. Which one would you rather live in, and why? Explain the method you would use to make the decision (by comparing…, by visiting…).
8.briefEs: Compara el loft y la casa toscana: ¿en cuál preferirías vivir y por qué? Usa would rather / would prefer y by + gerundio.
criteria: Use “would rather” and “would prefer” at least once each.
Use “by + gerund” to explain how you would decide.
Mention at least three facts from the cards.
Include one sentence with “although” or “whereas”.
8.model: If I had to choose, I'd rather live in the loft. Although the Tuscan house is bigger and more beautiful, it costs COP 3,800,000 a month plus COP 450,000 in utilities, whereas the loft costs COP 2,200,000. I live alone, so I don't need three bedrooms. I'd also prefer to be close to restaurants, transport and entertainment, and the loft has a great location in the city. Its industrial style, high ceilings and open spaces are exactly my taste. However, I would make the final decision by visiting both places at night, by checking how noisy the neighbourhood is, and by asking the neighbours about the building. If one day I have a family, I would prefer the Tuscan house, because it has more privacy, a garden and a peaceful natural environment. For now, the loft is the smarter choice.

8.title: Planning Dad's birthday
8.brief: Write an email to a brother or sister about a family party. State your preferences and explain how you could organise things.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un hermano sobre una fiesta familiar: expresa tus preferencias y explica cómo podríais organizarla.
criteria: At least two sentences with “would rather” and two with “would prefer”, with the correct patterns.
At least three “by + gerund” structures.
Use “instead of” and “to be keen on”.
8.model:
Hi Álvaro,

I'm planning Dad's fiftieth birthday, and I need your opinion. I'd prefer to have a small dinner at home, but Mum would rather book a restaurant. I'd rather not spend a lot of money, so we could save by cooking together and by making the cake ourselves. We could also invite the family by sending a group message instead of printing invitations. Would you prefer to organise the music or the decorations? I'm keen on the idea of a photo wall, which we could do by printing old pictures at home. I'd rather keep it a secret until the day itself. Let me know what you think.

Love,
Isa

8.title: Five ways to improve your English
8.brief: Write an article with practical tips to improve at something you know well. Explain the method for each tip and give a personal preference.
8.briefEs: Escribe un artículo con consejos prácticos para mejorar en algo que domines, explicando el método de cada uno y una preferencia personal.
criteria: At least five “by + gerund” structures.
One sentence with “would rather” and one with “would prefer”.
Use “instead of”, “to work out” and “worth doing”.
8.model:
Five ways to improve your English by yourself

You do not need an expensive course to make progress. First, you can improve your vocabulary by reading short articles every day and by writing down new words. Second, try to improve your listening by watching series with English subtitles instead of Spanish ones. Third, you can practise speaking by recording voice messages for a friend. Some people would rather study with a teacher, but I would prefer to learn at my own speed. Fourth, work out your weak points by checking your mistakes once a week. Finally, you can stay motivated by setting small goals. Learning a language gradually is worth doing, and it is much cheaper than you think. Most importantly, practising a little every day is better than studying for hours once a week.

8.title: Study alone or in a group?
8.brief: Write a forum post asking for advice about how to prepare for an exam. Say what you would rather do and what your friends would prefer.
8.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro pidiendo consejo sobre cómo preparar un examen: di qué preferirías tú y qué preferirían tus amigos.
criteria: At least two sentences with “would rather” and two with “would prefer”.
At least two “by + gerund” structures.
Use “method” and “to be keen on”.
8.model:
Hello everyone,

I have my final exams in June, and I can't decide how to prepare. I'd rather study alone because I concentrate better in silence. However, my friends would prefer to meet in the library every afternoon. I know that explaining things to others is a good method, and you can learn a lot by teaching a friend. On the other hand, I waste time by chatting when I'm in a group. I'm not very keen on long study sessions anyway. Would you rather study at home or in a library? Do you have any tips for making a good timetable? I'd prefer to hear from people who have done this before. Thanks!

Raúl

8.title: What shall we do tonight?
8.brief: Write a chat between two friends deciding what to do in the evening. They state their preferences and agree on how to decide.
8.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos que deciden qué hacer por la noche: expresan sus preferencias y acuerdan cómo decidir.
criteria: At least two sentences with “would rather” and one with “would prefer”.
At least one “by + gerund” structure.
Use “instead of”.
8.model:
Rosa: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?
Eli: I'd rather stay in. I'd prefer to watch something at home.
Rosa: OK. We could choose the film by voting.
