Eli: Good idea. I'd rather not watch a horror film, though!
Rosa: Fine. I'll bring the snacks instead of ordering pizza. See you at eight!

8.title: Online shops or real shops?
8.brief: Would you rather shop online or in the shops? Write an opinion essay explaining your preference and the methods you use to save money.
8.briefEs: ¿Preferirías comprar en línea o en tiendas? Escribe un ensayo de opinión con tu preferencia y los métodos que usas para ahorrar.
criteria: At least one “would rather” and one “would prefer”, correctly constructed.
At least three “by + gerund” structures.
Use “instead of”, “to be keen on” and “method”.
8.model:
Would you rather shop online or in the shops?

Most of my friends buy everything online, but I would rather go to the shops. I would prefer to try clothes on before I pay, because sizes are often different. You can also save money by comparing prices in different stores and by asking for discounts. Online shopping is convenient, and it is a good method when you are busy. However, I'm not keen on waiting for parcels that arrive late or damaged. Instead of ordering everything on a screen, I think we should support local shops. They give you personal advice, and they employ people from our neighbourhood. Personally, I enjoy walking around a shopping centre with friends at the weekend. In the end, we can find a balance by buying books and electronics online and clothes in the shops.

8.title: Our end-of-year trip
8.brief: Write a short proposal for a class trip. State what students and parents would prefer and explain how to organise and finance it.
8.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta breve para una excursión de clase: indica qué preferirían estudiantes y padres y explica cómo organizarla y financiarla.
criteria: At least one “would rather” and two “would prefer”.
At least three “by + gerund” structures.
Headings, “instead of”, “method” and “worth trying”.
8.model:
Proposal: our end-of-year trip

Introduction
This proposal suggests where Year 10 should go for the end-of-year trip.

The options
Most students would prefer to visit a theme park, but many parents would rather choose a cheaper and more educational place. I suggest a two-day visit to the science museum in Valencia, followed by a day at the beach.

How to organise it
We could reduce the cost by travelling by coach instead of by train. We could also raise money by selling cakes at school and by organising a quiz night. In my opinion, this method is worth trying because everyone would take part.

I would prefer to receive your decision by the end of the month.

9.title: Getting things done
9.brief: You are preparing your flat for a family visit. Write an email to a friend saying what you have had or are getting done by professionals.
9.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre lo que mandaste hacer o vas a mandar hacer en tu apartamento.
criteria: Four “have / get + object + past participle” structures in different tenses.
Use “quote / estimate” and “to service” or “to install”.
One sentence asking for advice.
9.model:
Hi Simón,

My parents are coming from Spain next month, so I'm getting my flat ready. Last week I had the walls painted and I got the windows cleaned. It was expensive, but it looks great! Tomorrow I'm having a new shower installed, because the old one was terrible. I also need to get the air conditioning serviced. I asked for two quotes: one company wants 300,000 pesos and the other 180,000. Have you ever had your AC fixed? Which company did you use? I'm also going to get my car washed before I pick them up at the airport.

Speak soon,
Lorena

9.title: Ideas for a better office
9.brief: Your manager asks for ideas to improve the office or classroom. Write a short proposal with suggestions using different structures.
9.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta corta con sugerencias para mejorar la oficina o el salón usando distintas estructuras.
criteria: Five suggestions with different forms: How about + -ing, Why don’t we, Maybe we could, One option is to, Have you thought about + -ing.
One negative question for a suggestion (Wouldn’t it be better to…?).
Use “worth a try” or “to go ahead”.
9.model:
Proposal: improving our office

After talking to the team, I would like to make some suggestions. First, how about creating a quiet room for people who need to concentrate? Many of us find the open space too noisy. Second, why don't we buy a few plants? It is a cheap idea, and research shows that plants make people happier. Maybe we could also change the lights near the windows, because they are too bright in the afternoon. One option is to have the coffee machine repaired instead of buying a new one. Have you thought about allowing people to work from home on Fridays? Wouldn't it be better to try it for one month first? I think these ideas are worth a try. If you agree, we can go ahead next week.

9.title: Talk me out of it
9.brief: Write a dialogue between two friends. One wants to do something risky (quit a job, buy an expensive car). The other makes suggestions to talk him or her out of it.
9.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo donde un amigo intenta convencer al otro de no hacer algo arriesgado con sugerencias.
criteria: Four suggestions in different forms (Why don’t you…? You could… What about…?).
One sentence with “get / have something done”.
Use “to talk someone into / out of”.
9.model:
Andrés: I've decided. I'm quitting my job tomorrow to travel around Asia.
Paula: Wait! Why don't you think about it for a week first?
Andrés: I've thought about it for months.
Paula: OK, but what about asking your boss for unpaid leave instead? You could travel for three months and come back.
Andrés: Hmm. That's not a bad idea.
Paula: And have you had your passport renewed? It expired last year, remember?
Andrés: Oh no, I forgot! I need to get it done.
Paula: See? Why not plan everything properly? Maybe you could save a bit more money first.
Andrés: You're trying to talk me out of it!
Paula: No, I'm trying to talk you into doing it well!

9.title: A new look for my room
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an email to a friend about changes you are having made in your room or home. Say what you have had done and make suggestions for a day together.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre los cambios que estás mandando hacer en tu habitación o casa y haz sugerencias para quedar.
criteria: At least four causative structures (have / get + object + past participle) in different tenses.
At least two suggestion forms (How about…, We could…, Why don’t we…).
Ask your friend a question with “Have you ever had…?”.
9.model:
Hi Camila,

Guess what? I'm having my bedroom redecorated next week! My dad is going to have the walls painted light green, and we're getting a new wardrobe built by a carpenter. I've also had the curtains made, because I couldn't find the right size in the shops. It's expensive, but I'm paying with the money from my summer job. How about coming over on Saturday to see it? We could order a pizza, or why don't we go to the cinema afterwards? Have you ever had your room painted? Tell me what you think I should do with the floor. Maybe I could get it covered with a rug.

See you soon,
Noelia

9.title: Where can I get my bike serviced?
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a forum post asking for advice about a repair or service. Say what you have had done before and what you want to get done now, and ask for suggestions.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un post de foro pidiendo consejo sobre una reparación o servicio: lo que mandaste hacer antes, lo que quieres hacer ahora y pide sugerencias.
criteria: At least three causative structures (had the brakes checked, get it serviced…).
At least two suggestion structures (Why don’t I…, How about…, Maybe I should…).
Use “to service” and finish with a request for advice.
9.model:
Hello everyone,

My bike has been making a strange noise for weeks, so I need to get it serviced before the summer. Last year I had the brakes checked in a shop near the station, but they charged me 60 euros, which seemed too much. Does anybody know a cheaper place? I'm also thinking of having a basket fitted on the front. Why don't I just do it myself? Well, the last time I tried to repair something, I had to get the whole wheel replaced! Maybe I should look for a repair workshop run by students. How about asking at the university noticeboard? Thanks in advance for your suggestions.

Ignacio

9.title: Improving our youth club
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a proposal to improve a youth club, sports centre or school. Use different suggestion forms and say what should be done by professionals.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una propuesta para mejorar un club juvenil, centro deportivo o colegio con distintas formas de sugerir y diciendo qué deberían hacer profesionales.
criteria: At least three causative structures with a past participle (have it repaired, get the walls painted).
At least four different suggestion forms (How about…, We could…, One option is to…, Why don’t we…).
Headings, and use “worth a try”.
9.model:
Proposal: improving our youth club

Introduction
The aim of this proposal is to suggest some improvements to the youth club, which is used by about sixty teenagers every week.

Suggestions
First, the roof leaks when it rains, so we should have it repaired before winter. How about getting the walls painted by volunteers to save money? We could also have a new table tennis table delivered, because the old one is broken. One option is to have wifi installed, which would help students who do their homework here. Why don't we ask local businesses to give us a discount? It might be worth having an electrician check the lights as well. We could also have the changing rooms cleaned by a professional company every month.

Conclusion
I believe these changes are worth a try, and I would be happy to organise them.

9.title: A cracked screen
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a chat between two friends. One has a broken phone and the other makes suggestions about getting it repaired.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un chat entre dos amigos: uno tiene el móvil roto y el otro le sugiere cómo hacerlo reparar.
criteria: At least three causative structures (get it replaced, have it done…).
At least two suggestion forms (Why don’t you…, How about…, You could…).
Between five and seven short messages, alternating speakers.
9.model:
Teo: My phone screen is cracked again.
Mia: Why don't you get it replaced at the shop on Park Road?
Teo: It's expensive. How about fixing it myself?
Mia: Last time you did that, you had to get the whole phone repaired!
Teo: True. I'll have it done on Saturday.
Mia: Great! You could also have a protective case fitted.

9.title: Ruined at the dry cleaner's
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a formal complaint about a service that went wrong (cleaning, repair, installation). Say what you had done and suggest two solutions.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una queja formal por un servicio que salió mal (limpieza, reparación, instalación): lo que mandaste hacer y dos soluciones que propones.
criteria: At least three causative structures with a past participle.
Two suggested solutions (You could…, I would like to suggest…).
Formal complaint register: I would be grateful if…, Yours faithfully.
9.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Last Monday I took my wool jacket to your shop on Gran Vía, because I wanted to have it cleaned before a family wedding. The assistant told me that I could get it back on Thursday. However, when I collected it, the jacket was stained and one sleeve had been shortened. I had trusted your shop to clean it carefully, and now I cannot wear it. I would like to suggest two solutions. You could have it repaired by a professional tailor and get the stain removed, or you could pay me the price of a new jacket, which is 85 euros. I would be grateful if you could reply by the end of the week.

Yours faithfully,
Sergio Marín

9.title: FixIt Phone Repairs
9.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a positive review of a repair shop or service. Explain what you had done there and recommend it with a suggestion.
9.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una reseña positiva de un taller o servicio: lo que mandaste hacer allí y recomiéndalo con una sugerencia.
criteria: At least four causative structures with a past participle.
One suggestion (why not…? / How about…?).
Use “quote” or “estimate” and “worth a try”.
9.model:
FixIt Phone Repairs: a great service

Last month my phone fell into the sink, and I thought it was finished. A friend suggested taking it to FixIt, so I had the battery and the screen checked there. The technician was friendly and honest. He explained that the screen needed replacing, so I got it replaced the same day. I also had a protective glass fitted for just 5 euros. The total price was 79 euros, which is cheaper than the quote I had received from another shop. If you have a broken phone, why not try them? It's definitely worth a try. Next time, I will have my phone insured as well!

10.title: My life in 2040
10.brief: Write about how you imagine your life and the world in 2040. Use will, the future continuous and the future perfect.
10.briefEs: Escribe cómo imaginas tu vida y el mundo en 2040 con will, futuro continuo y futuro perfecto.
criteria: Two future continuous verbs (will be living).
Three future perfect verbs (will have finished).
Use “by then” and “to be likely to”.
10.model: In 2040 I will be 42 years old. By then, I will have finished my master's degree and I will have worked in at least two countries. I imagine I will be living in a small house near the sea, and I will probably be working from home as a software engineer. I hope I will have started a family by that time. The world will also be very different. Most people will be driving electric cars, and many jobs will have disappeared because of artificial intelligence. Cities are likely to be hotter, so I think we will be spending more time indoors. However, I'm optimistic. I think we will have found solutions to some of the biggest environmental problems.

10.title: A timeline of my studies
10.brief: Write a short professional profile describing your education and work history. Use time expressions correctly.
10.briefEs: Escribe un perfil profesional corto con tu historial de estudios y trabajo usando expresiones de tiempo.
criteria: Use during, in, ago, from … to, for and since.
Mix past simple and present perfect correctly.
One sentence about future goals with “will have”.
10.model: I am a graphic designer from Manizales. I studied design at the National University from 2014 to 2019. During my studies, I worked part-time in a printing shop. In 2019, I moved to Bogotá and got a job at an advertising agency, where I worked for three years. I left that job two years ago to start my own studio. Since then, I have designed logos and websites for more than forty small businesses. I have also been teaching an evening course since 2023. My next milestone is to work with international clients. By the end of next year, I will have opened a small office and I will have hired my first employee.

10.title: Predictions for my city
10.brief: Write an article for a student magazine with predictions about your city in twenty years. Give reasons.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo con predicciones sobre tu ciudad en veinte años y da razones.
criteria: Two predictions with will / won’t and one with “be likely to”.
Two future continuous and two future perfect verbs.
Use “eventually” and “for the time being”.
10.model: What will Cali look like in twenty years? First, I think the city will have grown enormously: experts say the population is likely to reach four million. The new train to Jamundí will have been finished, so thousands of people will be commuting by rail instead of by car. Secondly, the climate will be hotter, and people will be living in buildings with green roofs and gardens. For the time being, salsa is the city's identity, and I don't think that will change. Eventually, Cali will become a centre for technology, and young people won't have left for Bogotá or abroad, because they will have good jobs at home.

10.title: My plans after the exams
10.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an email to a friend about your plans for the summer and the next year. Use the future continuous and the future perfect.
10.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre tus planes para el verano y el próximo año con futuro continuo y futuro perfecto.
criteria: At least two future continuous verbs (will be working…).
At least three future perfect verbs (will have saved…).
Use “by then” and “to be likely to”.
10.model:
Hi Rafa,

I can't believe the exams finish next week! This time next Friday I'll be sitting on a beach in Cádiz, and I won't be thinking about school at all. By the end of July, I will have saved enough money for my driving lessons because I'll be working in my uncle's shop every morning. In September I'm likely to be studying in Granada, so I'll be living away from home for the first time. By then, I will have met new people and I'll have learned to cook! Will you be working this summer? Perhaps we'll meet in August, before we both start university. Let me know your plans.

Cheers,
Enrique

10.title: Will robots take our jobs?
10.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an article about how work will change in the next ten years. Use will, the future continuous and the future perfect.
10.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un artículo sobre cómo cambiará el trabajo en los próximos diez años con will, futuro continuo y futuro perfecto.
criteria: At least two future continuous and three future perfect verbs.
Use “to be likely to” and “for the time being”.
One opinion with a reason in the last paragraph or sentence.
10.model:
Will robots take our jobs?

By 2035, many jobs will have changed completely. Experts say that robots are likely to do most of the repetitive work in factories and offices. This does not mean that people will be unemployed. In ten years' time, many workers will be using artificial intelligence to save time, and new jobs will have appeared that we cannot imagine today. For example, people will be designing virtual worlds, and others will be repairing robots. However, some skills will always be needed, such as creativity and teamwork. For the time being, nobody can say exactly what will happen. In my opinion, young people should learn how to adapt, because by the time we are thirty, the world of work will have changed again.

10.title: This time tomorrow
10.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a chat between two friends about a trip abroad. Use the future continuous and the future perfect with time markers.
10.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un chat entre dos amigos sobre un viaje al extranjero con futuro continuo y futuro perfecto y marcadores de tiempo.
criteria: At least two future continuous verbs.
At least two future perfect verbs.
Use a time marker with “by” or “in two weeks”.
10.model:
Alba: What will you be doing this time tomorrow?
Rubén: I'll be flying to Dublin! By the evening I will have arrived at my host family's house.
Alba: Lucky you! Will you be studying every day?
Rubén: Yes, but I'll be sightseeing at weekends. In two weeks I'll have visited the whole city.

10.title: Applying for a volunteer programme
10.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a formal letter applying for a volunteer programme. Describe your experience with past time expressions and your future plans with the future perfect and the future continuous.
10.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una carta formal para un programa de voluntariado: tu experiencia con expresiones de tiempo del pasado y tus planes con futuro perfecto y continuo.
criteria: At least four different past time expressions (during, in, from … to, for, since, ago).
At least one future continuous and one future perfect.
Formal register: Dear Sir or Madam and Yours faithfully.
10.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the summer volunteer programme at your wildlife centre. I am seventeen and I have been interested in animals since I was a child. During the last two years, I have helped at a local animal shelter every Saturday. I started there in 2023 and I worked in the kitchen for six months before moving to the dog area. From March to June this year, I also took a first-aid course. If I am accepted, I will be working with your team from July to August. By the end of the programme, I will have gained valuable experience, and I am likely to apply for a veterinary degree in the future. I would be very grateful for this opportunity.

Yours faithfully,
Aina Costa

10.title: Our class in ten years
10.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a forum post with predictions about your classmates and yourself in ten years. Use the future continuous and the future perfect.
10.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un post de foro con predicciones sobre tus compañeros y sobre ti dentro de diez años con futuro continuo y futuro perfecto.
criteria: At least two future continuous and two future perfect verbs.
Use “to be likely to” and “for the time being”.
Invite readers to add their own predictions.
10.model:
Hi everyone,

What will our class be doing in ten years' time? I'll start. Carlos will probably be playing football for a big club, because he has trained every day since he was nine. Lucía is likely to be running her own company, as she started selling bracelets online two years ago. As for me, by the time I'm twenty-six I will have finished my degree and I will be living in Mexico City. I won't have saved much money, but I'll be happy! For the time being, we are still in Year 10, and we only think about exams. Please add your own predictions below. The best one will win a prize!

Clara

10.title: My grandmother's life
10.brief: Write a short biography of a family member or someone you admire. Place each event in time with past time expressions and the right tenses.
10.briefEs: Escribe una biografía breve de un familiar o de alguien que admires situando cada hecho en el tiempo con expresiones de tiempo del pasado y los tiempos verbales correctos.
criteria: At least five different past time expressions (in, during, from … to, for, since, ago).
Simple past with finished time (in 1975, ago) and present perfect with since.
Events in chronological order, with at least four dates or periods.
10.model: My grandmother was born in a small village near Quito in 1952. During her childhood, she walked two hours to school every day. She left school in 1967 and worked in a textile factory for eight years. In 1975, she moved to Guayaquil, where she met my grandfather. They got married in 1978 and had three children from 1979 to 1985. Since 1991, she has run a small bakery in the city centre. She started the business thirty-five years ago with only fifty dollars, and today it has twelve employees. During the pandemic, she kept the shop open for the neighbours. She has never retired, and she says she never will. I admire her enormously.

11.title: A decision I would change
11.brief: Write about an important decision in your past. Explain the sequence of events, what you regret and what would have happened if you had decided differently.
11.briefEs: Escribe sobre una decisión importante, lo que lamentas y qué habría pasado si hubieras decidido distinto.
criteria: Three time clauses (as soon as, once, by the time, until).
Two sentences with should (not) have + past participle.
Two sentences with if + past perfect, would have + participle.
11.model: When I finished school, my parents wanted me to study law. As soon as I started the first semester, I knew it wasn't for me, but I didn't say anything until the third year. By the time I finally told them, I had spent a lot of money and time. I should have been honest from the beginning. I shouldn't have been so afraid of disappointing them. If I had changed to music earlier, I would have saved two years. In hindsight, though, the experience taught me something. Once I started studying music, I realised how important it is to follow your own path. If I hadn't studied law, I wouldn't have met my best friend.

11.title: Plans that fell through
11.brief: Write an email to a friend about a plan (a trip, a party, a business idea) that fell through. Explain the sequence and what you should have done.
11.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre un plan que fracasó, con la secuencia y lo que deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use “to fall through” and “with hindsight”.
Three time clauses with different conjunctions.
One regret with should have and one with if + past perfect.
11.model:
Hi Kate,

Remember the trip to Peru I told you about? Well, it fell through. The moment I booked the flights, things started to go wrong. Before I could reserve the hotels, my friend Mónica broke her leg. Then, once she had recovered, her company didn't give her the holidays. We waited until the last minute, and by the time we decided to cancel, the airline wouldn't give us our money back. With hindsight, I should have bought travel insurance. If I had checked the cancellation rules, I would have chosen a different ticket. Lesson learned!

Love,
Gabi

11.title: The story of a missed opportunity
11.brief: Write a story (real or invented) about someone who missed a great opportunity. End with what he or she learned.
11.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre alguien que perdió una gran oportunidad y lo que aprendió.
criteria: Four time clauses (before, after, once, the moment, until).
Two third conditional sentences.
Use “to turn down”, “to blame” or “otherwise”.
11.model: Carlos was a talented young footballer from Tumaco. When he was seventeen, a scout from a Brazilian club watched him play. The moment the match ended, the scout offered him a trial in São Paulo. But Carlos turned it down. He didn't want to leave his girlfriend, and he was afraid of living alone. After the scout left, his coach said, "You will regret this." He was right. A year later, Carlos's girlfriend left him, and he injured his knee before he could get another chance. He didn't play professionally until he was twenty-five, and by then it was too late. Carlos doesn't blame anyone. "If I had gone to Brazil, my life would have been different," he says. "Otherwise, I wouldn't be the coach I am now."

11.title: A late order
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] You run a small business and an order is late. Write a formal email to apologise, say what you should have done and explain what would have happened otherwise.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Tienes un pequeño negocio y un pedido llega tarde. Escribe un correo formal para disculparte, decir qué deberías haber hecho y qué habría pasado de otro modo.
criteria: At least three time clauses with different conjunctions (as soon as, by the time, once, until).
At least two sentences with should (not) have + past participle.
At least one third conditional sentence.
11.model:
Dear Mrs Gordon,

I am writing to apologise for the delay with your order of twenty cupcakes for your daughter's party. As soon as I realised the mistake, I called the supplier. Unfortunately, the flour had not arrived by the time we were supposed to start baking. I should have checked the delivery the day before, and I should not have promised you a fixed time. If I had ordered the ingredients earlier, I would have finished the cupcakes on time. Once the supplier delivers, we will bake the cupcakes immediately. I will not charge you anything until the order is complete. Please accept my sincere apologies.

Yours sincerely,
Bea Wilkins

11.title: The exam I almost missed
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a story about a day when you almost missed something important. Order the events with time clauses and finish with what you should have done.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una historia sobre un día en que casi pierdes algo importante: ordena los hechos con cláusulas de tiempo y termina con lo que deberías haber hecho.
criteria: At least four time clauses (the moment, as soon as, by the time, once, until).
At least one “should have + past participle”.
At least one third conditional sentence.
11.model: On the morning of my final maths exam, I woke up at nine instead of seven. The moment I looked at the clock, I jumped out of bed. I had forgotten to set my alarm because I had studied until two o'clock. I got dressed and ran to the bus stop, but the bus had already left. As soon as I realised this, I called my neighbour, who took me to school by car. By the time I reached the classroom, the exam had started. The teacher let me in, but I only had one hour instead of two. I should have gone to bed earlier. If I had set my alarm, I would have arrived calmly and I wouldn't have felt so nervous. Once the results arrived, I discovered that I had passed anyway.

11.title: Five lessons from my first job
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a blog post about the lessons you learned in a first job or activity. Use time clauses, regrets and one hypothetical past.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una entrada de blog sobre lo que aprendiste en un primer trabajo o actividad con cláusulas de tiempo, arrepentimientos y un pasado hipotético.
criteria: At least four time clauses with different conjunctions.
At least two sentences with should (not) have + past participle.
At least one third conditional sentence.
11.model:
Five lessons from my first job

Last summer, I worked in a busy ice-cream shop in Brighton, and I learned more than I expected. First, I should have asked questions at the beginning. Once I started asking, everything became easier. Second, I should not have arrived late on my first day. By the time I got there, my manager had already prepared the machines. Third, don't wait until the shop is crowded before you check the stock. As soon as customers started queuing, we ran out of strawberry ice cream! If I had planned better, we wouldn't have disappointed our customers. Of course, the job was tiring, and my feet hurt after every shift. Finally, remember to smile. The moment you smile, people feel welcome. I would do it again tomorrow, because I made friends and saved 800 pounds.

11.title: I missed the train
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a chat between two friends. One missed a train and regrets it. Use time clauses, a regret and a hypothetical past.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un chat entre dos amigos: uno perdió un tren y se arrepiente. Usa cláusulas de tiempo, un arrepentimiento y un pasado hipotético.
criteria: At least three time clauses (once, as soon as, until, when).
One “should have + past participle”.
One third conditional sentence.
11.model:
Jo: I should have checked the timetable! The train had already left when I got to the station.
Lena: Oh no. Once you reach the next station, call me.
Jo: I will. As soon as I arrive, I'll text you. If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have missed it.
Lena: Don't worry. Just wait until the next one comes.

11.title: Do we learn more from mistakes?
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an opinion essay about learning from mistakes. Include a personal example with time clauses, a regret and a hypothetical past.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre aprender de los errores con un ejemplo personal, cláusulas de tiempo, un arrepentimiento y un pasado hipotético.
criteria: At least three time clauses (once, by the time, until, when).
At least one “should have + past participle”.
At least one third conditional sentence.
11.model:
Do we learn more from our mistakes than from our successes?

I believe that mistakes teach us more, because we think harder after something goes wrong. Last year, I forgot to save my project before the computer shut down. Once I had lost three hours of work, I understood how important backups are. If I had never lost my work, I would not have learned that lesson. Of course, I should have saved the document every ten minutes, but it was too late. Some people say that success is a better teacher. They argue that when you win, you know what works. However, by the time we succeed, we have usually made many mistakes. Until we accept them, we cannot improve. In conclusion, I would not change my mistakes, because they made me who I am.

11.title: Why did we lose the final?
11.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a short report on why a team or project failed. Order events with time clauses and say what should have been done.
11.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un informe breve sobre por qué fracasó un equipo o proyecto: ordena los hechos con cláusulas de tiempo y di qué se debería haber hecho.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, What went wrong, Recommendations.
At least four time clauses and two “should have + past participle”.
At least one third conditional sentence.
11.model:
Report: our defeat in the basketball final

Introduction
This report explains why our school team lost the final on Saturday and suggests how to improve.

What went wrong
By the time the second quarter began, we were already ten points behind. The coach should have changed the players earlier, and we should have practised free throws more often. Once our best player was injured, the team lost confidence. If we had trained more during the week, we would have been stronger in the last minutes.

Recommendations
Until next season, we should train three times a week. As soon as the league starts, we will review our tactics after every match.

12.title: Why I'm learning English
12.brief: Write a paragraph explaining why you are learning English and what you want to use it for.
12.briefEs: Escribe un párrafo explicando por qué aprendes inglés y para qué lo quieres usar.
criteria: Three purpose structures: to + infinitive, so that, for + noun.
Three reason structures: because, since, due to, the reason why.
Use “to justify” or “rationale”.
12.model: There are several reasons why I am learning English. The main reason is my job: I work in tourism, and since most of our clients come from the USA and Europe, I need English to communicate with them. I also want to improve my English so that I can apply for a master's degree in Canada. Due to the high cost of studying abroad, I need a scholarship, and for that I must pass the IELTS exam. Another reason is personal. I love series and books, and I want to enjoy them in the original language. I spend about an hour a day studying, which is easy to justify because English opens so many doors.

12.title: A request for funding
12.brief: Write a formal email to your company or university asking for money for a project or course. Explain the purpose and the reasons.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal solicitando financiación para un proyecto o curso, explicando propósito y razones.
criteria: Use “so that”, “in order to” and “for + noun” for purpose.
Use “owing to”, “due to” and “because of” for reasons.
Formal register and a clear request.
12.model:
Dear Dr. Morales,

I am writing to request financial support of 2,500,000 pesos to attend the International Education Conference in Lima in October. The purpose of the trip is to present our research on bilingual education, so that other universities can learn from our experience. The money would be for the registration fee and accommodation. Owing to recent cuts in the department budget, I am unable to cover these costs myself. Due to the importance of the event, I believe it would be an excellent opportunity for the university. In order to share what I learn, I would organise a workshop for colleagues when I return. The reason I am applying now is that the deadline for registration is 15 August.

Yours sincerely,
Laura Castaño

12.title: What is it for?
12.brief: Describe an invention or app that you think is very useful. Explain what it is intended for and why it became popular.
12.briefEs: Describe un invento o aplicación útil: para qué sirve y por qué se volvió popular.
criteria: Use “to be intended for”, “for + -ing” and “so that”.
Three reason connectors (because of, since, the reason why).
Use “to account for” or “thereby”.
12.model: One app that I find extremely useful is a language exchange app. It is intended for people who want to practise a language with native speakers. You use it for chatting, sending voice messages and even making video calls, so that you can practise speaking without paying for classes. The reason why it became so popular is simple: it's free and fun. Since millions of people use it, you can always find a partner. Because of the pandemic, many people were at home and downloaded it, thereby helping it grow very fast. I think the social aspect accounts for its success: people don't only learn languages, they make friends from all over the world.

12.title: A charity run at school
12.brief: Write a formal email asking your head teacher for permission to organise an event. Explain the purpose and give your reasons.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal pidiendo permiso al director para organizar un evento: explica el propósito y da tus razones.
criteria: Purpose with to + verb, in order to and so that.
One purpose with for + person + to + verb.
Reasons with owing to and due to, in a formal register.
12.model:
Dear Mr Hendricks,

I am writing to ask for permission to organise a charity run at our school on 14 June. The purpose of the event is to raise money for the local animal shelter, so that the shelter can buy food and medicine for the winter. The run would take place in the school playground and the nearby park for the students to take part safely. Owing to the large number of participants, we would need the sports hall for registration. In order to cover the costs, we would sell water and snacks. Due to the success of last year's bake sale, we believe that many families will want to join us. I would also like to ask for two teachers to supervise the run. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Emma Clarke

12.title: A vegetable garden for our school
12.brief: Write a proposal for a project at your school or neighbourhood. Explain its purpose, justify it with reasons and say what you need.
12.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta para un proyecto de tu colegio o barrio: explica su propósito, justifícalo con razones y di qué necesitas.
criteria: Purpose with to + verb, so that and a negative purpose (in order not to).
Reasons with since, owing to and the reason why… is that.
Clear headings: Introduction, Reasons, What we need.
12.model:
Proposal: a vegetable garden for our school

Introduction
The purpose of this proposal is to ask the head teacher to approve a small vegetable garden behind the canteen.

Reasons
The garden is intended for students who want to learn about healthy food. Since the canteen throws away a lot of fruit peel, we could use it as compost. Owing to the lack of green areas in our school, many students spend break time on their phones. The reason why this project is worthwhile is that it brings students together.

What we need
We need a budget of 150 euros to buy tools and seeds. A volunteer group would take care of the garden so that it stays tidy. In order not to disturb lessons, the work would be done at lunchtime.

Thank you for considering this idea.

12.title: An app worth downloading
12.brief: Write a review of an app or gadget you use. Explain what it is for, why you use it and the reasons for its success or its problems.
12.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una aplicación o aparato que uses: para qué sirve, por qué lo usas y las razones de su éxito o sus problemas.
criteria: Purpose with “to be intended for”, “for + -ing” and “so that”.
At least three reason connectors (since, because, the reason why…).
Use “to account for” or “to avoid”.
12.model:
StudyBuddy: an app worth downloading

StudyBuddy is an app intended for students who want to organise their time. You use it for planning homework, setting reminders and tracking your progress. I downloaded it last term so that I could stop forgetting deadlines, and it has worked very well. The reason why I like it is that it's simple. Since it is free, you can try it without any risk. It accounts for the improvement in my marks, because I now finish my projects before the due date. The only problem is that it sends too many notifications, which can be annoying. Overall, it's a great tool for anyone who wants to avoid last-minute stress.

12.title: Why did you stop going to the gym?
12.brief: Write a chat between two friends. One explains why he or she changed a habit, giving the purpose and the reasons.
12.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos amigos: uno explica por qué cambió un hábito, dando el propósito y las razones.
criteria: Purpose with to + verb, for + -ing and so that.
Reasons with owing to and the reason is that.
Between four and six messages, alternating speakers.
12.model:
Ben: Why did you stop going to the gym?
Hana: Owing to my new timetable, I don't have time. I started running to save money.
Ben: What's the reason for that?
Hana: The reason is that the gym is expensive. I use an app for tracking my runs so that I can see my progress.

12.title: Should schools give homework?
12.brief: Should schools give homework? Write an opinion essay that explains the purpose of homework and your reasons for or against it.
12.briefEs: ¿Deben los colegios mandar deberes? Escribe un ensayo de opinión que explique el propósito de los deberes y tus razones a favor o en contra.
criteria: At least four purpose structures (to + verb, in order to, so that, for + person + to).
At least three reason connectors (owing to, since, the reason why…).
Use “to avoid” and a conclusion with a clear opinion.
12.model:
Should schools give homework?

Many people believe that homework is necessary, but I think it should be reduced. The main purpose of homework is to help students practise what they have learned. However, most students do it only in order to get a good mark, and they forget the content a week later. Owing to the amount of work, many teenagers sleep fewer hours than they need. The reason why this matters is that tired students cannot concentrate in class. Since we spend six hours at school, I think the rest of the day should be for rest and hobbies. Teachers could set short tasks for students to complete in class instead. This would avoid unnecessary stress, so that everybody could enjoy learning. For these reasons, schools should give less homework.

12.title: Why I left the school band
12.brief: Write a forum post explaining why you left a club, team or activity. Give the purpose of what you do now and your reasons.
12.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro explicando por qué dejaste un club, equipo o actividad: el propósito de lo que haces ahora y tus razones.
criteria: At least three purpose structures (to + verb, in order to, for + -ing, so that).
At least three reason connectors (due to, owing to, because, the reason why…).
Use “purpose” and “the reason why”.
12.model:
Hi everyone,

A lot of people have asked me why I left the school band, so here are my reasons. First, the main purpose of the band was to play at school events, but we practised for hours and performed only twice. Second, due to my exams, I couldn't attend every rehearsal. The reason why I decided to quit is that I felt stressed all the time. I stopped playing in order to concentrate on my studies, not because I don't like music. I still use my guitar for playing with friends, so that I don't lose my skills. Owing to the support of my teacher, I'm joining a smaller group next term. Thanks for reading!

Oliver

13.title: The mystery of the empty office
13.brief: Write a short mystery story. Someone finds an unusual situation and deduces what must, might or can't have happened.
13.briefEs: Escribe una historia de misterio en la que alguien deduce lo que debe, puede o no puede haber pasado.
criteria: Four past modals of certainty (must have, might have, could have, can’t have).
Use “evidence”, “to rule out” and “plausible”.
A clear ending with the solution.
13.model: When Diana arrived at the office on Monday, the door was open, the lights were on and her computer was missing. "Someone must have broken in," she thought. But there was no evidence of a robbery: the window wasn't broken and nothing else had been taken. It can't have been a stranger, because the alarm didn't go off. She ruled out the cleaner, who had been on holiday. "Maybe the IT guy took it for repairs," she thought. That seemed plausible, but he might have left a note. Then she saw a message on her phone from her boss: "Took your laptop home on Friday. Mine crashed. Sorry!" He must have forgotten to lock the door. Diana laughed — and then she was furious.

13.title: What should they have done?
13.brief: Read this situation: “A shop assistant accused a customer of stealing, but the customer was innocent.” Write your opinion about what the people should or shouldn’t have done.
13.briefEs: Opina sobre lo que las personas de una situación deberían o no deberían haber hecho.
criteria: Three past modals for judgments (should have, shouldn’t have, could have).
One past modal for certainty (must have felt).
Use “to give someone the benefit of the doubt” or “negligence”.
13.model: In my opinion, the shop assistant handled the situation badly. First, she shouldn't have accused the customer in front of other people. The customer must have felt terrible and embarrassed. The assistant should have given him the benefit of the doubt and checked the security cameras before saying anything. She could have called the manager or the security guard quietly. On the other hand, the manager should have trained the staff better, so there was some negligence from the shop too. The customer could have complained more strongly, but I think he reacted calmly. Finally, the shop ought to have apologised publicly. A small discount would have been a nice gesture.

13.title: A message about a mistake
13.brief: Something went wrong at a party you organised (food was missing, a guest got lost). Write an email to a friend guessing what happened and saying what you should have done.
13.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo especulando sobre qué salió mal en una fiesta y qué deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Use must have, might have and can’t have for guesses.
Use should have and shouldn’t have for regrets.
Include “presumably” or “to be bound to”.
13.model:
Hi Mario,

What a disaster yesterday! The cake didn't arrive, and I still don't know why. The bakery must have confused the address, because they say it was delivered at 6 p.m. It can't have gone to my flat — I was home all afternoon. It might have gone to the building across the street, which has a similar number. Presumably, someone there enjoyed a free chocolate cake! I should have given them my phone number. I also shouldn't have ordered it so late. Anyway, the guests didn't seem to mind. With so many people, something was bound to go wrong!

See you soon,
Clara

13.title: The mystery of the broken window
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a short mystery story set at school. Someone finds something unusual and deduces what must, might or can’t have happened.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe una historia de misterio ambientada en el colegio: alguien encuentra algo raro y deduce lo que debe, puede o no puede haber pasado.
criteria: At least four past modals of certainty (must have, could have, might have, can’t have).
Use “plausible” and “to rule out” or “evidence”.
A clear ending with the solution.
13.model: On Monday morning, the caretaker found a broken window in the science lab. There was glass on the floor, but nothing seemed to be missing. Mr Ford said that it must have happened over the weekend. The police found a football next to the glass. It could have been one of the students, but the school had been closed since Friday. It can't have been a burglar, because a burglar wouldn't have left a football. A child from the neighbourhood might have kicked it over the fence. Then Mr Ford noticed a small note inside the ball. It said that the local football club would pay for the damage. There was no other plausible explanation, so he ruled out any crime. The mystery was solved, and the club repaired the window.

13.title: Why didn't she come?
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an email to a friend wondering why a person missed an event. Guess what happened and say what you should have done.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un correo a un amigo preguntándote por qué alguien faltó a un evento: especula sobre lo ocurrido y di qué deberías haber hecho.
criteria: At least four past modals of certainty (must have, can’t have, might have, could have).
One regret with “should have”.
Use “presumably” or “to be bound to”.
13.model:
Hi Nina,

Yesterday's party was great, but I was a bit worried about Sara. She didn't come, and she didn't answer my messages. She must have forgotten about it, or maybe she got the wrong day. She can't have been ill, because I saw her on Friday and she looked fine. She might have gone to her grandparents' house, as she does every month. Presumably, her phone ran out of battery. I should have called her on Thursday to remind her. Her brother says she could have been at the cinema, but that seems unlikely because she hates horror films. Do you have any idea what happened? I'm bound to find out on Monday at school!

Love,
Diana

13.title: The school website crash
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a short report about a technical problem at school. Deduce the possible causes and judge the decisions that were taken.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un informe breve sobre un problema técnico del colegio: deduce las posibles causas y juzga las decisiones que se tomaron.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Possible causes, Judgement.
At least three deduction modals at different levels (must have, can’t have, might have).
At least three judgement modals (should have, could have, couldn’t have).
13.model:
Report: the school website crash

Introduction
This report looks at the possible causes of the website crash that happened on Monday, when students were trying to check their exam results.

Possible causes
The site must have received too many visits at the same time. It can't have been a virus, because the security team found no evidence of an attack. It might have been caused by a problem with the new server, although we cannot rule it out yet.

Judgement
The IT team should have tested the site before the results were published. They could have chosen a quieter time for the release. However, they couldn't have predicted the number of visitors.

13.title: Why hasn't he replied?
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a chat between two friends who try to guess why a classmate has not answered messages.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un chat entre dos amigos que intentan adivinar por qué un compañero no ha contestado a los mensajes.
criteria: At least four past modals of certainty (must have, might have, can’t have, could have).
One “should have”.
Use “presumably”.
13.model:
Gus: Sam hasn't replied to my messages all day.
Eva: He must have switched off his phone. He's got an exam tomorrow.
Gus: Or he might have lost it. He can't have gone out, because it's raining.
Eva: I should have asked him yesterday. We could have studied together.
Gus: Presumably he is revising, so let's not worry.

13.title: Could the accident have been avoided?
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an opinion essay about an accident or problem in your town. Say what people should or could have done and what must have caused it.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre un accidente o problema de tu ciudad: qué deberían o podrían haber hecho las personas y qué debió de causarlo.
criteria: At least three judgement modals (should have, shouldn’t have, could have, ought to have).
At least two deduction modals (might have, must have).
Use “to blame”, “negligence” or “the benefit of the doubt”.
13.model:
Could the accident have been avoided?

Last month, a cyclist was injured near my school when a car turned left without looking. In my opinion, the accident could have been avoided in several ways.

The driver should have checked his mirrors, and he shouldn't have been driving so fast near a school. The cyclist might have been wearing dark clothes, which would explain why the driver didn't see him. If so, he should have worn something bright and used lights. On the other hand, the council must have known that the junction was dangerous, because many people had complained about it. They ought to have installed a traffic light a long time ago. It is hard to say who is most to blame, but all three could have done more.

We must learn from this accident to protect cyclists in the future.

13.title: Who ate my lunch?
13.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write a forum post about a small mystery in your flat or school. Deduce what might have happened and judge your own decision.
13.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un post de foro sobre un pequeño misterio en tu piso o colegio: deduce lo que pudo pasar y juzga tu propia decisión.
criteria: At least four past modals of certainty (must have, can’t have, might have, could have).
One “should have”.
Use “the benefit of the doubt”.
13.model:
Hello everyone,

Something strange happened in the flat yesterday, and I need your help to solve it. I left a chicken sandwich in the fridge at nine in the morning, and when I came back at three, it had disappeared. It can't have been Marta, because she was at work all day. It must have been one of the boys, since they were the only people at home. Joe might have eaten it, although he says he didn't. There was a plate in the sink, so somebody must have had a late lunch. I should have written my name on it! If we give them the benefit of the doubt, it could have been a simple mistake. Please tell me what you think.

Iris

14.title: How it's made
14.brief: Describe the process of making a product you know well (chocolate, a T-shirt, arepas, bread). Use the passive and relative clauses.
14.briefEs: Describe el proceso de fabricación de un producto usando la voz pasiva y cláusulas relativas.
criteria: Six passive verbs describing stages.
One defining and one non-defining relative clause (with commas).
Use “stage”, “raw material” and “quality control”.
14.model: Chocolate is one of the products that Colombia is proud of. The raw material is cacao, which grows on trees in regions like Santander and Huila. At the first stage, the cacao pods are cut from the trees by hand and the beans are removed. Then the beans are fermented for about a week, which develops the flavour. After that, they are dried in the sun and sent to the factory. There, the beans are roasted and ground into a thick paste. Sugar and milk are added, and the mixture is heated and cooled several times. Before the chocolate is packed, quality control is carried out by experts whose job is to taste every batch. Finally, the bars are labelled and sold.

14.title: A recycling guide
14.brief: Write a short guide for your building explaining how rubbish is sorted and what happens to it.
14.briefEs: Escribe una guía corta para tu edificio explicando cómo se clasifica la basura y qué pasa con ella.
criteria: Five present passive verbs.
Two non-defining relative clauses with commas.
Use “to sort”, “to dispose of” and “to be labelled”.
14.model:
How our rubbish is sorted
In our building, rubbish is sorted into three groups. Plastic, glass and paper are put in the white bin, which is located next to the main door. Food waste is placed in the green bin. Everything else goes in the black bin. The bins are labelled clearly, so please check before you throw something away. The recyclable materials are collected every Tuesday by a group of local recyclers, who sell them to factories. Glass, which can be recycled many times, is taken to a plant in Soacha. Batteries and medicines must not be put in the bins; they are disposed of at the pharmacy on the corner. Thank you for helping!

14.title: A company I know
14.brief: Write a short profile of a company or business you know. Say what it does, how its products are made and who works there.
14.briefEs: Escribe el perfil de una empresa: qué hace, cómo se elaboran sus productos y quién trabaja allí.
criteria: Three passive verbs (are designed, is made, were founded).
Use who, which and whose in relative clauses.
One non-defining clause with commas.
14.model: Mochilas Wayuu Kanas is a small company that sells traditional bags online. It was founded in 2015 by Ana Epieyú, whose family has woven bags for generations. The bags are made by hand by a group of thirty women who live in La Guajira. Each bag, which can take up to three weeks to finish, is designed with traditional symbols. The cotton is bought from local farmers and the colours are chosen by the artisans. When the bags are ready, they are inspected, packed and sent to customers in more than ten countries. The company, which started with only two women, now supports many families in the community.

14.title: How a pizza is made at Luigi's
14.brief: Describe how a food or product is made in a place you know. Use the passive for the stages and add relative clauses with commas where appropriate.
14.briefEs: Describe cómo se prepara un alimento o producto en un lugar que conozcas, con pasivas para las etapas y cláusulas relativas con comas cuando corresponda.
criteria: At least six passive verbs describing stages.
One defining and one non-defining relative clause (with commas).
Use “raw materials”, “quality control” and sequence words (First, Then, Next, Finally).
14.model:
How a pizza is made at Luigi's

At Luigi's, a small restaurant that is famous in our town, every pizza is made by hand. First, the raw materials are checked every morning for quality. Then the dough is prepared with flour, water and yeast, and it is left to rest for twenty-four hours. Next, the dough is rolled out and covered with tomato sauce. The cheese, which is imported from Italy, is added after that. Once the toppings have been chosen by the customer, they are placed on the pizza. Finally, the pizza is baked in a wood oven for about ninety seconds. Quality control is carried out by the chef, who tastes every sauce before lunch. The pizzas that are not sold on the same day are given to a local charity.

14.title: Safety in the school science lab
14.brief: Write a short leaflet with safety rules for a lab, workshop or kitchen. Use modal passives for the rules and relative clauses to add information.
14.briefEs: Escribe un folleto corto con normas de seguridad para un laboratorio, taller o cocina, con pasivas modales y cláusulas relativas para añadir información.
criteria: At least six modal passives (must be, should be, has to be, must not be).
One defining and one non-defining relative clause (with commas).
Use “to dispose of” and “to be labelled”.
14.model:
Safety in the school science lab

Please read these rules before you start any experiment.
• Lab coats must be worn at all times.
• Long hair should be tied back.
• Safety glasses have to be put on before the equipment is switched on.
• Chemicals must not be tasted or smelled directly.
• Broken glass has to be reported to the teacher, who will dispose of it safely.
• Equipment that has been used must be cleaned and put back in the correct place.
• Waste liquids should be poured into the special containers, which are labelled in red.
• Mobile phones must not be used during the experiments.
If an accident happens, the teacher must be told immediately. Your safety is our priority!

14.title: Our visit to a bicycle factory
14.brief: Write an article for your school magazine about a visit to a factory or workshop. Describe the process with the passive and add information with relative clauses.
14.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para la revista del colegio sobre la visita a una fábrica o taller, describiendo el proceso con pasivas y añadiendo información con cláusulas relativas.
criteria: At least six passive verbs, one of them a modal passive.
At least two non-defining relative clauses with commas and one defining clause.
Use “stage” and sequence words (First, After that, Finally).
14.model:
Our visit to the Roca bicycle factory

Last Thursday, our class visited a bicycle factory in Zaragoza, which has been producing bikes since 1985. First, we learned that the frames are made of aluminium, which is lighter than steel. The metal tubes are cut by machines and then they are welded by experienced workers. After that, the frames are painted and left to dry for two hours. The wheels, which are produced in a different building, are fitted at the next stage. Each bike must be tested by an inspector before it is packed. The woman who showed us the factory explained that every unit is given a serial number. Finally, the bikes are sent to shops across Spain. It was an interesting trip, and I would recommend it.

14.title: How our school newspaper is produced
14.brief: Write a short report describing how something is produced in your school. Describe the steps in the passive and recommend one improvement.
14.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve que describa cómo se elabora algo en tu colegio, con los pasos en pasiva y una mejora recomendada.
criteria: At least six passive verbs in a clear sequence.
At least two modal passives (has to be approved, should be advertised).
One defining and one non-defining relative clause, and clear headings.
14.model:
Report: how our school newspaper is produced

Introduction
This report describes how the school newspaper, which is published every month, is produced.

The process
First, topics are chosen by the editorial team at a meeting. Then the articles are written by students who volunteer for the job. After that, the texts are corrected by two teachers, and the photos are selected. The pages are designed on computers that belong to the school. Before the newspaper is printed, it has to be approved by the head teacher. Finally, the copies are distributed in the corridors.

Recommendation
The newspaper should be advertised more widely, so that more students can join the team.

14.title: My job at the bakery
14.brief: Write an email to a friend explaining how your part-time job works. Describe the process in the passive and add information with relative clauses.
14.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo explicando cómo funciona tu trabajo de media jornada, con pasivas para el proceso y cláusulas relativas para añadir información.
criteria: At least six passive verbs in sequence.
At least one modal passive.
One defining and one non-defining relative clause with commas.
14.model:
Hi Alex,

You asked how the bread is made at the bakery where I work, so here is the process. At four in the morning, the flour is delivered by a van, and the ingredients are weighed. The dough is mixed in a big machine, which is cleaned every night. Then it is left to rise for an hour. Next, the loaves are shaped by hand by my boss, Mr Pons, who has worked there for thirty years. After that, they are baked at 220 degrees for forty minutes. The bread that is not sold by noon must be given away. I'm not allowed to use the oven yet, but I'm learning fast. Come and visit me one day!

Luis

14.title: How are jeans made?
14.brief: Write a chat in which one friend explains how a product is made. Use the passive and at least two relative clauses.
14.briefEs: Escribe un chat en el que un amigo explica cómo se fabrica un producto, con pasivas y al menos dos cláusulas relativas.
criteria: At least five passive verbs.
One defining and one non-defining relative clause.
Use “quality control”.
14.model:
Nadia: I watched a video about how jeans are made.
Joel: Really? Where is the cotton grown?
Nadia: It's grown in countries that are hot, like India. Then it's spun into thread, which is dyed blue.
Joel: And then?
Nadia: The fabric is cut and sewn, and the jeans are washed. Quality control is carried out at the end.

14.title: A tour of a pottery workshop
14.brief: Write a review of a guided tour of a workshop or factory. Describe the process you saw in the passive and give your opinion.
14.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una visita guiada a un taller o fábrica: describe el proceso que viste en pasiva y da tu opinión.
criteria: At least six passive verbs for the process.
One defining and two non-defining relative clauses with commas.
One positive opinion and one criticism.
14.model:
A fascinating tour of La Cerámica workshop

I visited this pottery workshop in Talavera with my class, and I loved every minute. The guide, who has been a potter for twenty years, showed us the whole process. First, the clay is collected from a local river and cleaned. Then it is shaped by hand or on a wheel, which is turned by the potter's foot. The pieces that have been made are dried for a week and baked in a kiln. Once they have cooled, they are painted with traditional patterns. Each piece must be checked before it is sold in the shop. The only problem was that the group was too big, so we couldn't see everything. Even so, it was worth the 8 euros.

15.title: Recommendations for my school
15.brief: Write a short report for the director of your school or company with recommendations to improve something. Use passive modals.
15.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve con recomendaciones para mejorar tu colegio o empresa usando modales pasivos.
criteria: Five passive modals (should be improved, must be repaired, ought to be offered).
Clear structure with headings: Introduction, Problems, Recommendations.
Use “priority”, “to address” and “feasible”.
15.model:
Introduction
This report presents the results of a survey of 80 students about the school cafeteria.

Problems
Most students said the food is too expensive and there are not enough healthy options. The queues are very long at lunchtime, and the tables are often dirty.

Recommendations
Our first priority should be prices. Cheaper menus should be offered to students who have lunch every day. Healthy options like salads and fruit must be added. The problem of the queues could be addressed by opening a second counter, which seems feasible. The tables ought to be cleaned after every break. Finally, students' opinions should be collected every semester. If these changes are made, the cafeteria will be much more popular.

15.title: A tricky opinion
15.brief: Write a dialogue between two colleagues discussing a new rule at work. They use tag questions to check the other person agrees.
15.briefEs: Escribe un diálogo entre dos colegas que comentan una regla nueva usando tag questions.
criteria: Five tag questions with correct auxiliaries.
Two passive modals (should be changed, can't be ignored).
Use “surely”, “to bring up” or “to bear in mind”.
15.model:
Ana: The new rule about arriving at 7:30 is terrible, isn't it?
Luis: It's a bit early, isn't it? But we can leave at 4:30.
Ana: True, but they didn't ask us first, did they?
Luis: No, they didn't. Surely that should have been discussed with the team.
Ana: Exactly. And parents with small children will have problems, won't they?
Luis: That's a good point. It can't be ignored. We should bring it up at the meeting, shouldn't we?
Ana: Definitely. The schedule ought to be changed for people with kids.
Luis: Let's bear in mind that the boss is under pressure too.
Ana: You always see both sides, don't you?
Luis: I try!

15.title: Advice for new drivers
15.brief: Write a leaflet with recommendations for new drivers in your city. Use passive modals and impersonal recommendations.
15.briefEs: Escribe un folleto con recomendaciones para conductores nuevos en tu ciudad con modales pasivos.
criteria: Five passive modals (must be worn, should be checked).
Use “It is recommended / advisable that…” once.
Use “ought to”, “have got to” or “urgent”.
15.model:
Driving in Bogotá: tips for beginners
Driving in a big city can be stressful, but these tips will help.
• Seat belts must be worn by everyone in the car, including passengers in the back.
• Your tyres and brakes should be checked every month.
• The "pico y placa" rules have got to be respected, or you will be fined.
• Mobile phones must not be used while driving.
• Extra time ought to be allowed for traffic jams, especially when it rains.
• It is advisable that long trips are planned with an app like Waze.
• Motorbikes can appear from anywhere, so mirrors should be used constantly.
Remember: patience is the most important skill on the road!

15.title: Improvements for Central Park
15.brief: Write a formal letter to a local councillor recommending improvements to a public space. Use passive modals of different strengths and one tag question.
15.briefEs: Escribe una carta formal a un concejal recomendando mejoras para un espacio público, con pasivas modales de distinta fuerza y una tag question.
criteria: At least five passive modals (should be, must be, ought to be, have to be, could be).
One tag question.
Use “surely” and “priority” or “to address”.
15.model:
Dear Councillor Reyes,

I am writing on behalf of the young people who use Central Park in our neighbourhood. In our opinion, several things should be done to improve it. First, the playground equipment must be repaired, because some of the swings are broken. The lights ought to be replaced as soon as possible, since the park is dangerous after dark. Bins should be placed near the benches, and they have to be emptied more often. A skate area could be built in the unused corner, which would be popular with teenagers. Surely the safety of children is a priority, isn't it? I hope these suggestions can be discussed at the next council meeting.

Yours sincerely,
Martín Vega

15.title: Tips for a new school
15.brief: Write an email to a friend who is starting at a new school. Give advice with passive modals and check your friend’s situation with tag questions.
15.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que empieza en un colegio nuevo: aconséjale con pasivas modales y comprueba su situación con tag questions.
criteria: At least five passive modals of different strengths.
At least three tag questions with the correct auxiliary.
Use “to bear in mind”.
15.model:
Hi Jana,

So, you're starting at your new school on Monday, aren't you? Here are my tips. The uniform has to be worn every day, so it should be washed on Sunday night. Homework must be handed in on time, or you'll lose marks. Your books ought to be covered with plastic, because they get dirty quickly. The canteen should be avoided at one o'clock, as it's very crowded. You haven't met the teachers yet, have you? They are strict, but they can be spoken to if you have a problem. The first week will be easier than you think, won't it? Just bear in mind that everybody feels nervous at the start!

Best of luck,
Cecilia

15.title: Match on Saturday
15.brief: Write a chat between two teammates who check the plans for a match. Use tag questions and passive modals.
15.briefEs: Escribe un chat entre dos compañeros de equipo que comprueban los planes de un partido, con tag questions y pasivas modales.
criteria: At least four tag questions with the correct auxiliary.
At least two passive modals (should be, must be, can’t be).
Use “surely”.
15.model:
Noa: The match is on Saturday, isn't it?
Yago: Yes. It should be played at ten, shouldn't it?
Noa: I think so. You haven't forgotten your boots, have you?
Yago: No! They must be cleaned first, though. You're coming to watch, aren't you?
Noa: Of course. Surely the team can't be beaten!

15.title: School starts too early
15.brief: Write a forum post giving your opinion about a school rule. Use passive modals for your recommendations and tag questions to invite agreement.
15.briefEs: Escribe un post de foro con tu opinión sobre una norma escolar, con pasivas modales para tus recomendaciones y tag questions para buscar acuerdo.
criteria: At least four tag questions with the correct auxiliary.
At least three passive modals.
Use “to bear in mind” or “surely”.
15.model:
Hi everybody,

School starts at 7.45 in my town, and I think it's far too early, don't you? Studies show that teenagers need more sleep, so lessons ought to be moved to nine o'clock. Of course, parents should be consulted first, shouldn't they? And the bus timetables would need to be changed, wouldn't they? I know that some teachers prefer early starts, but their opinion can't be the only one that counts, can it? In my opinion, a survey should be carried out among the students. The results must be shown to the head teacher, who might change her mind. You agree with me, don't you? Bear in mind that this is only my opinion.

Bruno

15.title: Improving the sports centre
15.brief: Write a proposal to improve a local sports or leisure centre. Use passive modals of different strengths, one tag question and one impersonal recommendation.
15.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta para mejorar un centro deportivo o de ocio con pasivas modales de distinta fuerza, una tag question y una recomendación impersonal.
criteria: At least five passive modals of different strengths.
One tag question and one “It is advisable that…”.
Headings: Introduction, Problems, Recommendations, and use “priority” and “feasible”.
15.model:
Proposal: improving the sports centre

Introduction
This proposal presents a few changes that should be made at our local sports centre, which is used by hundreds of young people.

Problems
The changing rooms are old, the showers are often cold, and the opening hours are too short. A lot of members have complained, haven't they?

Recommendations
The showers must be repaired as a matter of urgency. Safety must be treated as a priority, so the lights should be checked first. The changing rooms ought to be painted and cleaned every week. It is advisable that the opening hours are extended until ten o'clock. A new online booking system could be introduced to avoid long queues. All these changes are feasible, and they should be completed before the next school year begins.

I hope you will consider this proposal.

15.title: How to run a good study group
15.brief: Write a short article with advice on how to do something well in a group. Use passive modals for the rules and two tag questions to check your reader agrees.
15.briefEs: Escribe un artículo corto con consejos para hacer algo bien en grupo, con pasivas modales para las reglas y dos tag questions para comprobar que el lector está de acuerdo.
criteria: At least six passive modals (should be, must be, ought to be, have to be, can be).
At least two tag questions with the correct auxiliary.
Cover at least four practical areas (time and place, tasks, notes, breaks).
15.model:
How to run a good study group

Studying with friends can be very effective, but some rules should be followed. The time and place must be agreed in advance, and phones ought to be put away during the session. Every topic should be divided among the members, so that nobody is left with all the work. Difficult questions can be solved together, but answers must not be copied. The notes have to be shared by email after each meeting. Breaks should be taken every forty minutes, shouldn't they? Of course, the group should not be too big. Four members is a perfect number, isn't it? Finally, the group can be rewarded with a pizza when the exams are over!

15.title: Safety at the school bus stop
15.brief: Write a short report on a safety problem near your school. Describe the findings and recommend solutions with passive modals.
15.briefEs: Escribe un informe breve sobre un problema de seguridad cerca de tu colegio: describe lo observado y recomienda soluciones con pasivas modales.
criteria: Headings: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations.
At least four passive modals (should be, must be, ought to be, could be, has to be).
One tag question and “surely” or “priority”.
15.model:
Report: safety at the school bus stop

Introduction
This report looks at the safety of students who wait for the bus outside our school.

Findings
The pavement is narrow, and the road is busy at 3 p.m. Buses arrive in groups of three, so the area gets very crowded. Many students stand on the road, which can't be considered safe. The crossing is very faded.

Recommendations
A barrier should be installed along the pavement. The crossing must be repainted immediately, and a speed limit ought to be introduced near the school. Teachers could be asked to supervise the area for the first week. Surely this is a priority that has to be addressed before someone is hurt, isn't it?

16.title: My achievements this year

16.title: Looking back, looking forward
16.brief: Write a blog post looking back on your English learning so far and setting realistic goals for the future.
16.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre tu aprendizaje del inglés hasta ahora y metas realistas para el futuro.
criteria: Use “to look back on” and “in the long run”.
Two future perfect sentences with “by”.
One sentence with “would like to have + past participle”.

16.title: Big goals or small goals?
16.brief: [B1+ / puente a B2] Write an opinion essay about setting goals. Include a personal example with the present perfect and the simple past, and finish with goals using the future perfect.
16.briefEs: [B1+ / puente a B2] Escribe un ensayo de opinión sobre fijarse metas, con un ejemplo personal en present perfect y pasado simple, y termina con metas en futuro perfecto.
criteria: At least two present perfect and two simple past sentences with finished time.
One future perfect and one “would like to have + past participle”.
Use “in the long run” and “so far”.
16.model:
Should we set big goals or small goals?

Some people think that big goals motivate us more, but I prefer small ones. Last year, I decided to write a novel. I started in January, but by March I had written only ten pages, so I gave up. Since then, I have learned something important: small goals are more realistic. This year, I set a goal of writing one page a day, and so far I have completed sixty pages. In the long run, small steps lead to big results. Of course, big dreams are also useful. I would like to have published a story by the time I am eighteen, but I will not reach that goal unless I work every day. By next January, I will have finished the first draft if I keep going.
